black --include.rationale: Narrows which files are processed; does not change formatting behavior.

black --line-length.translation_modifier: using a specified maximum line length
black --line-length.rationale: Changes a formatting preference; does not affect file modification behavior.

black --quiet.rationale: Reduces output verbosity; does not change formatting behavior.

black --target-version.translation_modifier: formatting for a specified Python version
black --target-version.rationale: Changes which syntax features are used; does not affect file modification behavior.

bless --folder.translation_modifier: marking a directory as the blessed boot folder on the volume
bless --folder.rationale: Modifies the volume header to set the boot directory, changing boot behavior.

bless --info.translation_modifier: displaying the current boot configuration instead of changing it
bless --info.rationale: Read-only query that shows the blessed directory and boot device; modifies nothing.

bless --mount.translation_modifier: using the volume at the specified mount point
bless --mount.rationale: Only specifies which volume to operate on; the actual change requires --setBoot.

bless --nextonly.translation_modifier: applying the boot selection only for the next restart
bless --nextonly.rationale: Limits the boot change to a single restart, automatically reverting afterward.

bless --plist.translation_modifier: formatting the output as a property list
bless --plist.rationale: Only changes the output format; no state modification.

bless --setBoot.translation_modifier: setting the system to boot from the specified volume
bless --setBoot.rationale: Changes the startup disk, which determines which operating system loads on next reboot.

bless --unbless.translation_modifier: clearing the boot folder and file information from the volume
bless --unbless.rationale: Removes bootability from a volume, which may prevent it from being used as a startup disk.

bputil --remove.rationale: Deletes boot security policy; may prevent the system from booting.

brctl --all.rationale: Displays information about all iCloud Drive documents.

brew cleanup --prune.translation_modifier: removing all cache files older than the specified number of days
brew cleanup --prune.rationale: Widens the scope of cache deletion based on age.

brew cleanup -s.translation_modifier: also removing the download cache for the latest versions
brew cleanup -s.rationale: Removes all cached downloads, not just outdated ones; forces re-downloading on next install.

brew deps --installed.translation_modifier: showing dependencies for all installed formulas
brew deps --installed.rationale: Widens the scope of the listing; still read-only.

brew deps --tree.translation_modifier: displaying dependencies in a tree structure
brew deps --tree.rationale: Changes the output format; still read-only.

brew install --HEAD.translation_modifier: installing the latest development version from the source repository
brew install --HEAD.rationale: Development versions may be unstable and introduce regressions or breaking changes.

brew install --build-from-source.translation_modifier: compiling from source code instead of using a pre-built binary
brew install --build-from-source.rationale: Builds locally; slower but does not increase risk beyond the standard install.

brew install --cask.translation_modifier: installing a macOS application instead of a command-line formula
brew install --cask.rationale: Installs a graphical application; may require elevated permissions for system integration.

brew install --force.rationale: Replaces already-installed software, which may disrupt dependent tools or configurations.

brew link --force.translation_modifier: linking even if the formula is keg-only
brew link --force.rationale: Overrides the keg-only restriction, which may conflict with system-provided software.

brew link --overwrite.translation_modifier: overwriting existing files in the Homebrew prefix
brew link --overwrite.rationale: Replaces existing files with symbolic links, which may break other installations.

brew reinstall --cask.translation_modifier: reinstalling a macOS application instead of a command-line formula
brew reinstall --cask.rationale: Reinstalls a graphical application; may require elevated permissions.

brew uninstall --force.translation_modifier: removing all versions of the formula and ignoring dependencies
brew uninstall --force.rationale: Removes all installed versions and skips dependency checks, which may break other installed software.

brew uninstall --zap.translation_modifier: also removing all associated files, preferences, and caches
brew uninstall --zap.rationale: Performs aggressive cleanup that deletes application data and configuration beyond the formula itself.

brew upgrade --force.translation_modifier: reinstalling even if already at the latest version
brew upgrade --force.rationale: Re-runs installation scripts unnecessarily; may disrupt currently working software.

brew upgrade --greedy.translation_modifier: also upgrading casks that auto-update themselves
brew upgrade --greedy.rationale: Expands upgrade scope to include auto-updating casks that would normally be skipped.

brotli --force.translation_modifier: overwriting existing output files without prompting
brotli --force.rationale: Overwrites existing output files without confirmation; recoverable from backups.

brotli --rm.translation_modifier: removing the source file after successful compression or decompression
brotli --rm.rationale: Permanently deletes the original input file, making recovery dependent on backups.

brotli -d.rationale: Decompresses .br files, creating or replacing the original file.

brotli -f.rationale: Silently overwrites existing output files without confirmation, which can cause data loss.

bunzip2 --force.translation_modifier: overwriting existing output files without prompting
bunzip2 --force.rationale: Overwrites existing output files without confirmation; recoverable from backups.

bzip2 -1.translation_modifier: using fastest compression with a smaller block size
bzip2 -1.rationale: Changes compression level only; does not affect which files are processed.

bzip2 -9.translation_modifier: using maximum compression with a larger block size
bzip2 -9.rationale: Changes compression level only; does not affect which files are processed.

bzip2 -c.translation_modifier: writing output to standard output and keeping the original file
bzip2 -c.rationale: Leaves the original file intact; output goes to standard output.

bzip2 -d.rationale: Decompresses .bz2 files in place, replacing them with the original content.

bzip2 -f.rationale: Forces compression even if the output file already exists.

bzip2 -k.translation_modifier: keeping the original file instead of replacing it
bzip2 -k.rationale: Preserves the source file; a safety-enhancing option.

bzip2 -q.rationale: Suppresses warning messages; does not change behavior.

bzip2 -s.translation_modifier: using less memory at the cost of slower speed
bzip2 -s.rationale: Reduces memory usage; does not change which files are processed.

bzip2 -t.translation_modifier: testing the integrity of compressed files without decompressing
bzip2 -t.rationale: Read-only operation that verifies compressed file integrity.

bzip2 -v.rationale: Displays compression ratio for each file; does not change behavior.

bzip2 -z.translation_modifier: forcing compression regardless of how the command was invoked
bzip2 -z.rationale: Overrides the default behavior based on invocation name; same risk as normal compression.

caffeinate -d.rationale: Prevents the display from sleeping, which only affects power management behavior temporarily.

caffeinate -i.rationale: Keeps the system awake during idle periods.

caffeinate -m.translation_modifier: preventing the disk from idle sleeping
caffeinate -m.rationale: Keeps the disk spinning during idle periods; only affects power management.

caffeinate -s.translation_modifier: preventing the system from sleeping while plugged in
caffeinate -s.rationale: Keeps the system awake only when plugged in; ends when the command exits.

caffeinate -t.translation_modifier: for a specified number of seconds
caffeinate -t.rationale: Limits the duration; the assertion expires automatically.

caffeinate -u.translation_modifier: declaring that the user is active and turning on the display
caffeinate -u.rationale: Wakes the display as if user activity occurred; temporary assertion.

caffeinate -w.rationale: Ties the sleep prevention to the lifetime of another process.

cal -3.translation_modifier: showing the previous, current, and next month
cal -3.rationale: Displays a three-month view; read-only output.

cal -A.translation_modifier: including the specified number of months after the current month
cal -A.rationale: Extends the calendar display forward; read-only output.

cal -B.translation_modifier: including the specified number of months before the current month
cal -B.rationale: Extends the calendar display backward; read-only output.

cal -h.rationale: Cosmetic change that removes the highlight on the current day.

cal -j.translation_modifier: numbering days from the start of the year instead of the month
cal -j.rationale: Changes display format to show day-of-year numbers; read-only output.

cal -m.rationale: Displays a single named month; read-only output.

cal -y.rationale: Displays all twelve months; read-only output.

cancel -E.translation_modifier: using an encrypted connection to the print server
cancel -E.rationale: Only changes connection security; does not affect which jobs are canceled.

cancel -a.translation_modifier: canceling all jobs on all printers
cancel -a.rationale: Removes every pending print job across all printers at once.

cancel -h.translation_modifier: connecting to a specific print server
cancel -h.rationale: Only changes which server is contacted.

cancel -u.translation_modifier: canceling all jobs owned by a specific user
cancel -u.rationale: Removes all pending jobs for one user; those jobs must be resubmitted.

cancel -x.translation_modifier: also deleting the job data files
cancel -x.rationale: Removes the stored print data in addition to canceling, making recovery impossible.

cargo add --build.rationale: Marks the dependency for use during compilation only; still just modifies Cargo.toml.

cargo add --dev.rationale: Marks the dependency for development use only; still just modifies Cargo.toml.

cargo build --release.translation_modifier: with optimizations enabled for a production build
cargo build --release.rationale: Produces an optimized binary; only changes the build profile.

cargo build --target.translation_modifier: for a specific platform target instead of the host
cargo build --target.rationale: Cross-compiles for another platform; does not change what is modified.

cargo build --workspace.translation_modifier: for all packages in the workspace
cargo build --workspace.rationale: Extends the build to every package in the workspace; still a local compilation.

cargo clippy --fix.translation_modifier: automatically applying suggested fixes to the source code
cargo clippy --fix.rationale: Modifies source files in place to apply lint fixes; changes may be incorrect.

cargo doc --no-deps.translation_modifier: only for this package, excluding dependencies
cargo doc --no-deps.rationale: Reduces the scope of documentation generated; still a local operation.

cargo doc --open.translation_modifier: opening the documentation in a web browser after building
cargo doc --open.rationale: Opens a local HTML file; no additional files are modified.

cargo fix --allow-dirty.translation_modifier: even if the working directory has uncommitted changes
cargo fix --allow-dirty.rationale: Bypasses the clean working directory check, risking loss of uncommitted edits if fixes overlap.

cargo fix --allow-staged.translation_modifier: even if there are staged changes in the repository
cargo fix --allow-staged.rationale: Bypasses the staged-changes check; auto-fixes may conflict with staged modifications.

cargo fmt --check.translation_modifier: only checking whether code is formatted without making changes
cargo fmt --check.rationale: Reports formatting issues without modifying any files.

cargo install --force.translation_modifier: overwriting an existing installation of the same binary
cargo install --force.rationale: Replaces a previously installed binary without confirmation.

cargo publish --allow-dirty.translation_modifier: allowing publication from a working directory with uncommitted changes
cargo publish --allow-dirty.rationale: Bypasses the clean working directory check, risking publication of unintended changes.

cargo publish --dry-run.translation_modifier: simulating the upload without actually publishing
cargo publish --dry-run.rationale: No package is uploaded; only performs validation checks.

cargo publish --no-verify.rationale: Bypasses the pre-publish build check, risking publication of a broken package.

cargo run --release.translation_modifier: with optimizations enabled for a production build
cargo run --release.rationale: Only changes the build profile; does not change what the program does.

cargo test --no-fail-fast.translation_modifier: running all tests even if some fail
cargo test --no-fail-fast.rationale: Changes test runner behavior; does not affect what is modified.

cargo test --no-run.translation_modifier: compiling the tests without actually running them
cargo test --no-run.rationale: Only compiles; no test code is executed.

cargo test --release.rationale: Only changes the build profile used for test compilation.

cargo test --workspace.translation_modifier: for all packages in the workspace
cargo test --workspace.rationale: Extends testing to every package in the workspace; still a local operation.

cargo update --dry-run.translation_modifier: simulating the update without actually changing the lock file
cargo update --dry-run.rationale: No files are modified; only shows what would change.

cargo yank --undo.translation_modifier: reversing a previous yank to make the version available again
cargo yank --undo.rationale: Restores availability of a previously yanked version; a corrective action.

cat -b.rationale: Numbers only non-blank lines; still read-only.

cat -e.translation_modifier: showing non-printing characters and marking the end of each line
cat -e.rationale: Combines -v with end-of-line markers; still read-only.

cat -n.rationale: Adds line numbers to output; still read-only.

cat -s.translation_modifier: squeezing multiple consecutive blank lines into one
cat -s.rationale: Reduces repeated blank lines in output; still read-only.

cat -t.translation_modifier: showing non-printing characters and displaying tabs as ^I
cat -t.rationale: Combines -v with visible tab characters; still read-only.

cat -v.translation_modifier: showing non-printing characters as visible placeholders
cat -v.rationale: Makes control characters visible; still read-only.

cc -D.translation_modifier: defining a preprocessor variable before compilation
cc -D.rationale: Sets a compile-time constant; affects how source code is interpreted but modifies nothing on disk.

cc -E.translation_modifier: only running the preprocessor without compiling
cc -E.rationale: Stops after preprocessing and prints the expanded source; does not produce compiled output.

cc -I.translation_modifier: adding a directory to search for included header files
cc -I.rationale: Expands the search path for header files; does not modify any files.

cc -O2.rationale: Enables most compiler optimizations; affects generated code quality but not source files.

cc -O3.rationale: Enables additional optimizations that may increase code size; does not modify source files.

cc -S.translation_modifier: producing assembly code instead of a compiled program
cc -S.rationale: Stops after generating assembly language output; does not link or execute.

cc -Wall.rationale: Turns on warning messages during compilation; does not change what is built.

cc -Werror.translation_modifier: treating all warnings as errors that stop compilation
cc -Werror.rationale: Causes compilation to fail on warnings; prevents output but does not destroy anything.

cc -c.translation_modifier: compiling without linking into a final program
cc -c.rationale: Produces an intermediate object file instead of a finished program; narrower scope than the default.

cc -g.translation_modifier: including debugging information in the output
cc -g.rationale: Adds debug data to the compiled output; increases file size but has no destructive effect.

cc -l.rationale: Tells the linker to include a library; does not modify the library itself.

cc -o.translation_modifier: writing the output to a specific file
cc -o.rationale: Names the output file; overwrites an existing file of the same name, but this is expected behavior.

cc -v.translation_modifier: showing the commands run during each compilation step
cc -v.rationale: Displays verbose compilation details; does not change behavior.

cd -L.translation_modifier: following symbolic links instead of resolving them
cd -L.rationale: Default behavior on most shells; does not modify any files.

cd -P.translation_modifier: resolving symbolic links to use the physical directory path
cd -P.rationale: Changes how the path is resolved; does not modify any files.

certtool -v.rationale: Only increases the amount of output displayed.

certtool C -P.translation_modifier: skipping creation if a system identity already exists for the domain
certtool C -P.rationale: Prevents overwriting an existing identity; a safety check.

certtool c -a.translation_modifier: generating the private key with a default access control list
certtool c -a.rationale: Allows other applications to access the key; widens access scope.

certtool c -c.translation_modifier: creating the keychain if it does not already exist
certtool c -c.rationale: Creates a new keychain file if needed; does not overwrite existing keychains.

certtool c -k.rationale: Selects a non-default keychain; does not change the operation.

certtool c -p.translation_modifier: providing the keychain passphrase on the command line
certtool c -p.rationale: Supplies the passphrase non-interactively; does not change the operation.

certtool c -u.translation_modifier: limiting private key access to the current user only
certtool c -u.rationale: Restricts key access; a security-enhancing option.

chmod +a.translation_modifier: adding an access control list entry to the file
chmod +a.rationale: Grants or restricts additional access beyond standard Unix permissions.

chmod -C.translation_modifier: returning whether the file's access control list is correct without making changes
chmod -C.rationale: Read-only check of ACL correctness; does not modify anything.

chmod -E.translation_modifier: reading access control list entries from standard input
chmod -E.rationale: Replaces ACL entries with those read from input; the scope depends on the input provided.

chmod -H.translation_modifier: following symbolic links on the command line but not in subdirectories
chmod -H.rationale: Causes permission changes to affect the targets of explicitly named symbolic links when used with -R.

chmod -L.translation_modifier: following all symbolic links during recursive traversal
chmod -L.rationale: When combined with -R, permission changes can reach files outside the intended directory tree via symbolic links.

chmod -N.translation_modifier: removing all access control list entries from the file
chmod -N.rationale: Strips all ACL entries, reverting the file to standard Unix permissions only.

chmod -P.translation_modifier: without following any symbolic links during recursive traversal
chmod -P.rationale: The default behavior with -R; avoids reaching files outside the directory tree.

chmod -R.rationale: Applies permission changes to an entire directory tree, greatly increasing the blast radius.

chmod -a.translation_modifier: removing an access control list entry from the file
chmod -a.rationale: Revokes a specific access control list entry, which may remove needed access.

chmod -f.translation_modifier: suppressing error messages for files that cannot be changed
chmod -f.rationale: Silences errors but does not change what permissions are modified.

chmod -h.translation_modifier: changing the permissions of the symbolic link itself instead of its target
chmod -h.rationale: Targets the link rather than the linked file; a narrower scope change.

chmod -i.translation_modifier: removing inherited access control list entries
chmod -i.rationale: Strips inherited ACL entries, which may change effective permissions on the file.

chmod -v.translation_modifier: showing each file as its permissions are changed
chmod -v.rationale: Adds verbose output without changing what permissions are modified.

chown -H.translation_modifier: following symbolic links on the command line but not in subdirectories
chown -H.rationale: Causes ownership changes to affect the targets of explicitly named symbolic links when used with -R.

chown -L.translation_modifier: following all symbolic links during recursive traversal
chown -L.rationale: When combined with -R, ownership changes can reach files outside the intended directory tree via symbolic links.

chown -P.translation_modifier: without following any symbolic links during recursive traversal
chown -P.rationale: The default behavior with -R; avoids reaching files outside the directory tree.

chown -R.rationale: Applies ownership changes to an entire directory tree, greatly increasing the blast radius.

chown -f.translation_modifier: suppressing error messages for files that cannot be changed
chown -f.rationale: Silences errors but does not change what ownership is modified.

chown -h.translation_modifier: changing the ownership of the symbolic link itself instead of its target
chown -h.rationale: Targets the link rather than the linked file; a narrow scope change.

chown -n.translation_modifier: interpreting owner and group as numeric IDs instead of names
chown -n.rationale: Changes how the owner and group arguments are parsed but does not affect scope.

chown -v.translation_modifier: showing each file as its ownership is changed
chown -v.rationale: Adds verbose output without changing what ownership is modified.

chown -x.rationale: Limits the scope of recursive traversal to the current filesystem.

chroot -G.translation_modifier: running the command with multiple specified groups' permissions
chroot -G.rationale: Assigns multiple group memberships to the command, potentially widening its access within the new root.

chroot -g.translation_modifier: running the command with a specified group's permissions
chroot -g.rationale: Changes the group permissions for the command, which may grant or restrict access to files in the new root.

chroot -u.translation_modifier: running the command as a specified user
chroot -u.rationale: Changes which user account the command runs under, altering its permissions inside the new root.

cksum -o.translation_modifier: using a specified historic checksum algorithm instead of the default
cksum -o.rationale: Only changes which checksum algorithm is used; no state modification.

clang -O2.rationale: Increases optimization level; does not change the compilation model.

clang -Wall.rationale: Adds diagnostic messages; does not change generated code.

clang -c.translation_modifier: compiling to object files without linking
clang -c.rationale: Produces object files only; does not create an executable.

clang -o.translation_modifier: writing the output to a specified file
clang -o.rationale: Specifies the output filename; may overwrite an existing file at that path.

claude --dangerously-skip-permissions.translation_modifier: bypassing all permission checks before executing actions
claude --dangerously-skip-permissions.rationale: Allows the AI to execute any tool without user approval, including destructive file and system operations.

claude --model.rationale: Selects which model to use; does not change available capabilities.

claude -c.rationale: Resumes an existing session; does not change capabilities.

claude -p.translation_modifier: printing a single response and exiting without interactive mode
claude -p.rationale: Runs in non-interactive mode; useful for scripting.

claude -r.translation_modifier: resuming a specific conversation by session ID
claude -r.rationale: Resumes an existing session; does not change capabilities.

clusterdb --all.translation_modifier: operating on all databases in the cluster
clusterdb --all.rationale: Affects every database in the PostgreSQL cluster, greatly increasing blast radius.

clusterdb-17 --all.translation_modifier: operating on all databases in the cluster
clusterdb-17 --all.rationale: Affects every database in the PostgreSQL cluster, greatly increasing blast radius.

codesign --all-architectures.translation_modifier: verifying each architecture in a universal binary separately
codesign --all-architectures.rationale: Thorough verification across all architectures; read-only.

codesign --check-notarization.translation_modifier: checking whether the code has been notarized by Apple
codesign --check-notarization.rationale: Read-only online check of notarization status.

codesign --continue.translation_modifier: continuing to process remaining files even if one fails
codesign --continue.rationale: Changes error handling behavior; does not change the operation on individual files.

codesign --deep.translation_modifier: signing or verifying all nested code bundles recursively
codesign --deep.rationale: Extends the operation to all embedded frameworks and plugins.

codesign --dryrun.translation_modifier: simulating the signing operation without writing any changes
codesign --dryrun.rationale: No files are modified; only shows what would happen.

codesign --entitlements.translation_modifier: embedding entitlements in the code signature
codesign --entitlements.rationale: Entitlements grant capabilities to the application; incorrect values may grant excessive permissions.

codesign --ignore-resources.rationale: Speeds up verification but may miss corrupted resources; read-only operation.

codesign --keychain.translation_modifier: searching for the signing identity in a specific keychain
codesign --keychain.rationale: Selects a non-default keychain; does not change the signing operation.

codesign --options.translation_modifier: setting runtime enforcement options such as hardened runtime or library validation
codesign --options.rationale: Controls security policies enforced on the signed code at runtime.

codesign --remove-signature.rationale: Leaves the application unsigned; it may be blocked by Gatekeeper or fail to run.

codesign --timestamp.translation_modifier: including a secure timestamp from Apple's timestamp service
codesign --timestamp.rationale: Adds a trusted timestamp; improves signature validity over time.

codesign --validate-constraint.translation_modifier: validating launch environment constraints on the code

codesign -D.translation_modifier: writing a detached signature to a separate file
codesign -D.rationale: Creates a separate signature file; the original code is not modified.

codesign -R.translation_modifier: checking the signature against a specified requirement
codesign -R.rationale: Read-only verification against a custom requirement; does not modify the code.

codesign -d.translation_modifier: displaying signature information instead of signing

codesign -f.rationale: Overwrites the current signature, which may invalidate existing trust settings.

codesign -h.translation_modifier: displaying the hosting chain of a running process
codesign -h.rationale: Read-only inspection of process signing state.

codesign -i.translation_modifier: setting a custom identifier string in the signature
codesign -i.rationale: Overrides the default identifier; only meaningful during signing.

codesign -o.translation_modifier: setting option flags in the code signature
codesign -o.rationale: Embeds runtime options that affect how the system enforces signing policies.

codesign -r.translation_modifier: embedding internal requirements in the code signature
codesign -r.rationale: Sets requirements that must be met for the signature to be considered valid.

codesign -s.translation_modifier: signing the code with a specified identity
codesign -s.rationale: Applies a code signature that determines whether the application is trusted.

codesign -v.rationale: Read-only validation of the signature; does not modify the application.

column -c.translation_modifier: fitting output to a specific display width
column -c.rationale: Only changes how output is formatted; read-only operation.

column -s.translation_modifier: using a custom character to separate columns
column -s.rationale: Only changes how input is parsed; read-only operation.

column -t.translation_modifier: detecting columns automatically and creating a table
column -t.rationale: Only changes how output is formatted; read-only operation.

column -x.translation_modifier: filling columns before rows instead of the default order
column -x.rationale: Only changes the order in which entries are arranged; read-only operation.

comm -1.translation_modifier: hiding lines that only appear in the first file
comm -1.rationale: Only changes which lines are displayed; read-only operation.

comm -2.translation_modifier: hiding lines that only appear in the second file
comm -2.rationale: Only changes which lines are displayed; read-only operation.

comm -3.translation_modifier: hiding lines that appear in both files
comm -3.rationale: Only changes which lines are displayed; read-only operation.

comm -i.rationale: Only changes how lines are compared; read-only operation.

compress -b.translation_modifier: limiting the compression code size to a specified number of bits
compress -b.rationale: Only tunes the compression algorithm; no change in what files are affected.

compress -c.translation_modifier: writing compressed output to the terminal instead of replacing the file
compress -c.rationale: Leaves the original file unmodified; only writes to the terminal.

compress -f.translation_modifier: overwriting existing files without asking for confirmation
compress -f.rationale: Suppresses confirmation prompts and forces compression even when the file would grow.

compress -v.translation_modifier: showing the compression ratio for each file
compress -v.rationale: Only adds informational output; no change to behavior.

cp -H.translation_modifier: following symbolic links on the command line but not in subdirectories
cp -H.rationale: Only follows symbolic links explicitly named as arguments; limited scope expansion.

cp -L.translation_modifier: following all symbolic links and copying their targets
cp -L.rationale: Copies the files that symbolic links point to, which may pull in files outside the intended scope.

cp -P.translation_modifier: preserving symbolic links as links instead of copying their targets
cp -P.rationale: Copies the link itself rather than following it; this is the default in recursive mode.

cp -R.rationale: Copies entire directory trees, increasing the scope of files potentially overwritten at the destination.

cp -a.translation_modifier: in archive mode, preserving all file attributes and recursing into directories
cp -a.rationale: Combines recursive copy with metadata preservation, mirroring entire directory trees.

cp -c.translation_modifier: using copy-on-write clones when supported by the filesystem
cp -c.rationale: Creates lightweight clones that share storage until modified; falls back to normal copy if unsupported.

cp -f.translation_modifier: removing and recreating destination files that cannot be overwritten
cp -f.rationale: Forcefully replaces destination files without prompting, even if permissions would normally prevent it.

cp -i.rationale: Adds an interactive confirmation step, reducing the risk of accidental overwrite.

cp -l.translation_modifier: creating hard links instead of copying file contents
cp -l.rationale: Creates hard links rather than independent copies; changes to one affect the other.

cp -p.translation_modifier: preserving file timestamps, permissions, and ownership
cp -p.rationale: Maintains original file metadata; does not change the copy scope.

cp -r.rationale: Same as -R; copies entire directory trees, increasing the scope of files potentially overwritten.

cp -s.translation_modifier: creating symbolic links instead of copying file contents
cp -s.rationale: Creates symbolic links rather than copies; the original file remains unchanged.

cp -v.translation_modifier: showing each file as it is copied
cp -v.rationale: Adds verbose output without changing what is copied.

cp -x.rationale: Limits the scope of recursive copying to the current filesystem.

cpio --insecure.translation_modifier: allowing extraction through symbolic links and absolute paths
cpio --insecure.rationale: Disables path safety checks, allowing files to be written anywhere on the filesystem via symbolic link or absolute path traversal.

cpio -F.translation_modifier: reading from or writing to a specified archive file instead of standard input or output
cpio -F.rationale: Changes the archive source or destination; does not add destructive capability.

cpio -L.translation_modifier: following symbolic links and archiving the files they point to
cpio -L.rationale: Changes which data is archived but does not add destructive capability.

cpio -d.translation_modifier: creating directories as needed during extraction
cpio -d.rationale: Ensures required directories exist; does not add destructive capability.

cpio -i.rationale: Extracts archive contents to disk, which may overwrite existing files.

cpio -l.translation_modifier: creating hard links instead of copying files
cpio -l.rationale: Uses links instead of copies in pass-through mode; no data is destroyed.

cpio -m.rationale: Only affects file timestamps; does not change what is extracted.

cpio -o.translation_modifier: creating a new archive from a list of files
cpio -o.rationale: Writes a new archive to standard output; does not modify existing files.

cpio -p.translation_modifier: copying files directly to a destination directory
cpio -p.rationale: Copies files to a target directory, potentially overwriting files at the destination.

cpio -t.rationale: Read-only operation that only displays filenames from the archive.

cpio -u.translation_modifier: overwriting newer files on disk with older archived versions
cpio -u.rationale: Unconditionally replaces existing files regardless of modification time, which can cause data loss.

cpio -v.rationale: Only adds verbose output listing each file processed.

createdb -D.rationale: Sets the default tablespace; a storage configuration choice.

createdb -E.rationale: Sets the character encoding for the new database; a configuration choice.

createdb -O.rationale: Sets the owner of the new database; a configuration choice during creation.

createdb -T.translation_modifier: cloned from a specified template database
createdb -T.rationale: Uses a template as the starting point; does not modify the template itself.

createdb -U.rationale: Specifies the authentication identity; the user's permissions determine what is allowed.

createdb -e.translation_modifier: displaying the SQL commands being sent to the server
createdb -e.rationale: Shows the generated SQL; read-only diagnostic output.

createdb -h.translation_modifier: on a specified database server host
createdb -h.rationale: Specifies which server to connect to; does not change the operation.

createdb -l.rationale: Sets the locale for the new database; a configuration choice.

createdb -p.rationale: Specifies which port to connect on; does not change the operation.

crontab -e.translation_modifier: opening the task schedule in a text editor for changes
crontab -e.rationale: Allows editing scheduled tasks that take effect immediately after saving.

crontab -l.rationale: Read-only display of scheduled tasks; modifies nothing.

crontab -r.translation_modifier: removing all scheduled tasks without asking for confirmation
crontab -r.rationale: Deletes every scheduled task at once with no confirmation prompt; recovery requires manually recreating each entry.

crontab -u.translation_modifier: targeting a specific user's task schedule instead of your own
crontab -u.rationale: Operates on another user's scheduled tasks, which may affect services or jobs that user depends on.

csplit -f.translation_modifier: using a custom prefix for the output file names
csplit -f.rationale: Only changes the naming of output files; does not affect what is split.

csplit -k.translation_modifier: keeping already-created files if an error occurs
csplit -k.rationale: Prevents cleanup of partial output, which is safer than the default behavior of deleting them.

csplit -n.translation_modifier: using a custom number of digits in the output file names
csplit -n.rationale: Only changes the naming of output files; does not affect what is split.

csplit -s.translation_modifier: suppressing the display of output file sizes
csplit -s.rationale: Only hides informational output; does not change what files are created.

cups-config --cflags.translation_modifier: showing compiler options needed to build against CUPS

cups-config --datadir.translation_modifier: showing the default CUPS data directory
cups-config --datadir.rationale: Read-only display of a directory path.

cups-config --ldflags.translation_modifier: showing linker options needed to build against CUPS

cups-config --libs.translation_modifier: showing the libraries needed to link against CUPS

cups-config --serverbin.translation_modifier: showing the directory where CUPS filters and backends are stored
cups-config --serverbin.rationale: Read-only display of a directory path.

cups-config --serverroot.translation_modifier: showing the directory where CUPS configuration files are stored
cups-config --serverroot.rationale: Read-only display of a directory path.

cups-config --static.translation_modifier: reporting static libraries instead of shared libraries
cups-config --static.rationale: Only changes which library names are displayed.

cups-config --version.translation_modifier: showing the installed CUPS version number

cupsaccept -E.translation_modifier: using an encrypted connection to the print server
cupsaccept -E.rationale: Only changes connection security; does not affect queue behavior.

cupsaccept -U.rationale: Only changes the username used for authentication.

cupsaccept -h.translation_modifier: connecting to a specific print server
cupsaccept -h.rationale: Only changes which server is contacted.

cupsctl --debug-logging.rationale: Only increases log verbosity; does not change print behavior.

cupsctl --no-debug-logging.rationale: Only reduces log verbosity; does not change print behavior.

cupsctl --no-remote-admin.rationale: Restricts administration to the local machine, reducing the attack surface.

cupsctl --no-remote-any.translation_modifier: restricting printing to local network addresses only
cupsctl --no-remote-any.rationale: Limits who can submit print jobs, reducing exposure.

cupsctl --no-share-printers.translation_modifier: stopping the sharing of local printers with other computers
cupsctl --no-share-printers.rationale: Hides printers from the network; only affects discoverability.

cupsctl --no-user-cancel-any.translation_modifier: preventing users from canceling print jobs owned by other users
cupsctl --no-user-cancel-any.rationale: Restricts job cancellation to the job owner, which is the safer default.

cupsctl --remote-admin.rationale: Opens the print server to remote configuration changes, which could be exploited on an untrusted network.

cupsctl --remote-any.translation_modifier: allowing printing from any network address
cupsctl --remote-any.rationale: Opens the print server to connections from the entire network, including the internet.

cupsctl --share-printers.translation_modifier: sharing local printers with other computers
cupsctl --share-printers.rationale: Makes local printers visible and usable on the network.

cupsctl --user-cancel-any.translation_modifier: allowing users to cancel print jobs owned by other users
cupsctl --user-cancel-any.rationale: Lets any user remove another user's print jobs from the queue.

cupsdisable --hold.translation_modifier: holding remaining jobs until the printer is re-enabled
cupsdisable --hold.rationale: Preserves queued jobs instead of discarding them; they resume when the printer is re-enabled.

cupsdisable -E.translation_modifier: using an encrypted connection to the print server
cupsdisable -E.rationale: Only changes connection security; does not affect printer state.

cupsdisable -c.translation_modifier: canceling all pending jobs on the printer
cupsdisable -c.rationale: Removes every queued job on the printer; those jobs must be resubmitted.

cupsdisable -r.translation_modifier: setting a reason message for why the printer is stopped
cupsdisable -r.rationale: Only sets a display message; does not change printer behavior.

cupsenable --release.rationale: Resumes jobs that were held; equivalent to unpausing the queue.

cupsenable -E.translation_modifier: using an encrypted connection to the print server
cupsenable -E.rationale: Only changes connection security; does not affect printer state.

cupsenable -c.translation_modifier: canceling all pending jobs on the printer
cupsenable -c.rationale: Removes every queued job on the printer; those jobs must be resubmitted.

cupsreject -E.translation_modifier: using an encrypted connection to the print server
cupsreject -E.rationale: Only changes connection security; does not affect queue behavior.

cupsreject -U.rationale: Only changes the username used for authentication.

cupsreject -h.translation_modifier: connecting to a specific print server
cupsreject -h.rationale: Only changes which server is contacted.

cupsreject -r.translation_modifier: setting a reason message shown to users whose jobs are rejected
cupsreject -r.rationale: Only sets a display message; does not change rejection behavior.

curl --compressed.translation_modifier: requesting a compressed response and automatically decompressing it
curl --compressed.rationale: Negotiates transfer compression for efficiency; does not change what data is sent or received.

curl --connect-timeout.translation_modifier: limiting the time allowed to establish a connection
curl --connect-timeout.rationale: Sets a timeout; does not change what data is sent or received.

curl --create-dirs.translation_modifier: creating any missing local directories needed by the output path
curl --create-dirs.rationale: Creates intermediate directories for -o output; does not change what data is transferred.

curl --data-binary.translation_modifier: sending data exactly as specified without any processing
curl --data-binary.rationale: Transmits raw binary data to a remote server, which may include sensitive content.

curl --insecure.rationale: Long form of -k; disables server identity verification, exposing the connection to interception or man-in-the-middle attacks.

curl --location-trusted.translation_modifier: following HTTP redirects automatically while sending credentials to every redirected host
curl --location-trusted.rationale: Sends the username and password to all hosts in the redirect chain, which may leak credentials to unintended servers.

curl --no-clobber.translation_modifier: skipping the download if the output file already exists
curl --no-clobber.rationale: Prevents overwriting existing files, reducing the risk of accidental data loss.

curl --retry.translation_modifier: retrying the request a specified number of times on failure
curl --retry.rationale: Repeats the request on transient failures; does not change the operation's scope.

curl -F.translation_modifier: sending data as a multipart form upload
curl -F.rationale: Transmits form data including file contents to a remote server.

curl -H.rationale: Adds a header to the request; may carry authentication tokens but does not change the operation's scope.

curl -I.translation_modifier: fetching only the HTTP headers without the body
curl -I.rationale: Reduces the amount of data retrieved; does not increase risk.

curl -L.rationale: Follows server-issued redirects, which is standard behavior for most web requests.

curl -O.translation_modifier: saving the response to a file named by the remote server
curl -O.rationale: Writes to a filename controlled by the remote server, which could overwrite unexpected local files.

curl -T.translation_modifier: uploading a local file to the server
curl -T.rationale: Sends local file contents to a remote destination, which may expose sensitive data.

curl -X.rationale: Changes the HTTP verb but does not inherently increase risk beyond the base command.

curl -b.rationale: Includes cookie data in the request; does not change the operation's scope.

curl -c.translation_modifier: saving received cookies to a file
curl -c.rationale: Writes cookie data to a local file; low risk as cookies are small metadata.

curl -d.translation_modifier: sending data in an HTTP request body
curl -d.rationale: Transmits data to a remote server, which may include sensitive information.

curl -f.translation_modifier: failing silently on HTTP server errors
curl -f.rationale: Suppresses error document output on failure; does not change what data is sent or received.

curl -k.rationale: Disables server identity verification, exposing the connection to interception or man-in-the-middle attacks.

curl -m.translation_modifier: limiting the total time allowed for the entire operation
curl -m.rationale: Sets a maximum duration; does not change the operation's scope.

curl -o.translation_modifier: saving the response to a specified local file
curl -o.rationale: Writes remote content to the local filesystem, which could overwrite existing files.

curl -s.translation_modifier: hiding progress output and error messages
curl -s.rationale: Suppresses informational output but does not change the operation's behavior or scope.

curl -u.translation_modifier: authenticating with a username and password
curl -u.rationale: Sends credentials to the server; may expose them if the connection is not encrypted.

curl -v.translation_modifier: showing verbose connection and transfer details
curl -v.rationale: Increases output detail for debugging; does not change the operation.

curl -w.translation_modifier: displaying specified transfer metrics after completion
curl -w.rationale: Only adds informational output; does not change the operation.

curl -x.translation_modifier: routing the request through a specified proxy server
curl -x.rationale: Redirects traffic through a proxy; does not change what data is sent.

cut -b.rationale: Chooses which bytes to display; still read-only.

cut -c.rationale: Chooses which characters to display; still read-only.

cut -d.translation_modifier: using a specified character to separate fields
cut -d.rationale: Changes which character marks field boundaries; still read-only.

cut -f.rationale: Chooses which fields to display; still read-only.

cut -s.translation_modifier: skipping lines that do not contain the delimiter
cut -s.rationale: Filters out lines without delimiters; still read-only.

cut -w.translation_modifier: using whitespace as the field separator
cut -w.rationale: Treats spaces and tabs as a single separator; still read-only.

date -u.translation_modifier: displaying or setting time in UTC instead of local time
date -u.rationale: Changes the timezone for display; does not modify the system clock.

dbiprof --delete.translation_modifier: deleting the profiling data after displaying it
dbiprof --delete.rationale: Removes the profiling data file; data is lost if not saved elsewhere.

dbiprof5.34 --delete.translation_modifier: deleting the profiling data after displaying it
dbiprof5.34 --delete.rationale: Removes the profiling data file; data is lost if not saved elsewhere.

dc -I.rationale: Only changes how input numbers are interpreted; read-only computation.

dc -O.rationale: Only changes how results are displayed; read-only computation.

dc -S.translation_modifier: setting the decimal precision to a specified number of places
dc -S.rationale: Only changes calculation precision; read-only computation.

dc -e.rationale: Runs a calculation from the command line instead of interactively; read-only.

dc -f.translation_modifier: reading commands from a specified file
dc -f.rationale: Processes calculations from a file; does not modify the file.

dc -i.rationale: Enables interactive prompts; no effect on data or files.

dc -x.translation_modifier: enabling extended register mode for more storage slots
dc -x.rationale: Expands available register names; no effect on files or data safety.

dd bs=.translation_modifier: using a specified block size for reading and writing
dd bs=.rationale: Changes the I/O block size; does not affect what data is written.

dd conv=noerror.translation_modifier: continuing past read errors instead of stopping
dd conv=noerror.rationale: Silently skips unreadable data, which may produce incomplete or corrupted output.

dd conv=notrunc.rationale: Preserves existing data beyond what is written; a safety-improving option.

dd conv=swab.translation_modifier: swapping every pair of input bytes
dd conv=swab.rationale: Transforms data byte order; does not add destructive capability.

dd conv=sync.translation_modifier: padding each input block to the full block size
dd conv=sync.rationale: Pads short reads with null bytes; useful with noerror for disk recovery.

dd count=.translation_modifier: copying only a specified number of blocks
dd count=.rationale: Limits the amount of data copied; a scope-reducing option.

dd ibs=.translation_modifier: using a specified input block size
dd ibs=.rationale: Sets the read block size independently; does not affect what data is written.

dd if=.translation_modifier: reading from a specified input file or device
dd if=.rationale: Specifies the data source; does not add destructive capability.

dd obs=.translation_modifier: using a specified output block size
dd obs=.rationale: Sets the write block size independently; does not affect what data is written.

dd of=.translation_modifier: writing to a specified output file or device
dd of=.rationale: Directs raw data to a target that may be a disk device, overwriting all existing content without confirmation.

dd seek=.translation_modifier: skipping a specified number of blocks from the beginning of the output before writing
dd seek=.rationale: Changes the write offset, which may leave gaps or overwrite data at arbitrary positions in the output.

dd skip=.translation_modifier: skipping a specified number of blocks from the beginning of the input
dd skip=.rationale: Changes the read offset; does not add destructive capability.

dd status=none.rationale: Only suppresses informational messages; does not change behavior.

dd status=progress.translation_modifier: showing transfer progress once per second
dd status=progress.rationale: Only changes what status information is displayed.

defaults delete -app.translation_modifier: looking up the application by name instead of its preference domain
defaults delete -app.rationale: Only changes how the application is identified; does not affect the deletion.

defaults delete -g.translation_modifier: deleting from the global preferences shared by all applications
defaults delete -g.rationale: Removes a global preference that affects all applications, which may cause widespread behavior changes.

defaults read -app.translation_modifier: looking up the application by name instead of its preference domain
defaults read -app.rationale: Only changes how the application is identified; still a read-only operation.

defaults read -currentHost.translation_modifier: limited to preferences for the current computer only
defaults read -currentHost.rationale: Only narrows which preferences are read; still a read-only operation.

defaults read -g.translation_modifier: reading from the global preferences shared by all applications
defaults read -g.rationale: Only changes which preference domain is read; still a read-only operation.

defaults write -app.translation_modifier: looking up the application by name instead of its preference domain
defaults write -app.rationale: Only changes how the application is identified; does not affect the value being written.

defaults write -array.translation_modifier: setting the value as a list, replacing any existing list
defaults write -array.rationale: Overwrites the entire list value for the key, which could discard existing entries.

defaults write -array-add.translation_modifier: adding items to the end of an existing list value
defaults write -array-add.rationale: Appends to the existing list without removing current entries.

defaults write -bool.translation_modifier: setting the value as a true-or-false type
defaults write -bool.rationale: Only specifies the data type of the value; does not change the scope of the write.

defaults write -currentHost.translation_modifier: limited to preferences for the current computer only
defaults write -currentHost.rationale: Narrows the scope of the write to the current computer, reducing blast radius.

defaults write -dict.translation_modifier: setting the value as a set of key-value pairs, replacing any existing set
defaults write -dict.rationale: Overwrites the entire set of key-value pairs, which could discard existing entries.

defaults write -dict-add.translation_modifier: adding key-value pairs to an existing set without removing current entries
defaults write -dict-add.rationale: Merges new pairs into the existing set without discarding current data.

defaults write -float.translation_modifier: setting the value as a decimal number type
defaults write -float.rationale: Only specifies the data type of the value; does not change the scope of the write.

defaults write -g.translation_modifier: writing to the global preferences shared by all applications
defaults write -g.rationale: Changes a global preference that affects all applications, widening the blast radius.

defaults write -int.translation_modifier: setting the value as a whole number type
defaults write -int.rationale: Only specifies the data type of the value; does not change the scope of the write.

defaults write -string.translation_modifier: setting the value as a text type
defaults write -string.rationale: Only specifies the data type of the value; does not change the scope of the write.

df -H.rationale: Displays sizes in human-readable units using powers of 1000; still read-only.

df -T.translation_modifier: showing only volumes of a specified type
df -T.rationale: Filters output to specific volume types; still read-only.

df -Y.rationale: Adds a column showing each volume's storage type; still read-only.

df -a.translation_modifier: including all mounted volumes, even hidden system ones
df -a.rationale: Shows additional mount points that are normally hidden; still read-only.

df -c.translation_modifier: showing a grand total across all volumes
df -c.rationale: Adds a summary total row to the output; still read-only.

df -h.rationale: Displays sizes in human-readable units like megabytes and gigabytes; still read-only.

df -i.translation_modifier: including counts of used and free file slots
df -i.rationale: Adds file-slot usage statistics to the output; still read-only.

df -k.rationale: Shows sizes in kilobyte blocks; still read-only.

df -l.translation_modifier: showing only locally attached storage volumes
df -l.rationale: Filters out network-mounted volumes; still read-only.

diff --color.rationale: Adds color highlighting to the output; purely cosmetic.

diff -B.translation_modifier: ignoring changes that only add or remove blank lines

diff -N.translation_modifier: treating missing files as empty when comparing directories
diff -N.rationale: Shows full content of files that exist in only one directory; still read-only.

diff -a.translation_modifier: treating all files as text even if they appear to contain non-text data
diff -a.rationale: Forces text comparison mode; still read-only.

diff -b.translation_modifier: ignoring changes in the amount of whitespace
diff -b.rationale: Treats multiple spaces as equivalent to one; still read-only.

diff -c.translation_modifier: showing differences in context format with surrounding lines
diff -c.rationale: Changes the output format; still read-only.

diff -d.translation_modifier: trying harder to find the smallest possible set of differences
diff -d.rationale: Uses more processing power for a more precise result; still read-only.

diff -i.translation_modifier: ignoring differences between uppercase and lowercase letters
diff -i.rationale: Loosens the comparison criteria; still read-only.

diff -p.translation_modifier: showing which function each change appears in
diff -p.rationale: Adds function context to the output; still read-only.

diff -q.translation_modifier: only reporting whether files differ, not showing the details

diff -r.translation_modifier: recursively comparing all files in subdirectories
diff -r.rationale: Extends comparison to entire directory trees; still read-only.

diff -u.translation_modifier: showing differences in unified format with context lines
diff -u.rationale: Changes the output format; still read-only.

diff -w.rationale: Ignores spaces and tabs when comparing; still read-only.

diff -y.translation_modifier: showing the two files side by side
diff -y.rationale: Changes the output layout; still read-only.

dig +answer.translation_modifier: displaying the answer section of the response
dig +answer.rationale: Controls which output section is shown; still read-only.

dig +comments.translation_modifier: including comment lines in the output

dig +dnssec.translation_modifier: requesting DNS security validation records in the response
dig +dnssec.rationale: Requests additional security-related DNS records; still read-only.

dig +multiline.translation_modifier: printing records in a verbose multi-line format
dig +multiline.rationale: Changes output format for readability; still read-only.

dig +noall.rationale: Disables output sections; typically combined with +answer to show only results.

dig +norecurse.translation_modifier: sending a non-recursive query to the server
dig +norecurse.rationale: Requests that the server not perform recursion; still read-only.

dig +notcp.translation_modifier: using UDP instead of TCP for the query
dig +notcp.rationale: Explicitly uses UDP transport; still a read-only query.

dig +nsid.translation_modifier: requesting the name server identifier from the responding server
dig +nsid.rationale: Asks the server to include its identifier; still read-only.

dig +nssearch.translation_modifier: finding all authoritative name servers and showing their SOA records
dig +nssearch.rationale: Queries multiple servers for zone authority information; still read-only.

dig +recurse.translation_modifier: requesting recursive resolution from the server
dig +recurse.rationale: The default behavior; asks the server to resolve the query fully.

dig +retry.translation_modifier: setting the number of retry attempts for failed queries
dig +retry.rationale: Controls retry behavior; still a read-only query.

dig +short.translation_modifier: showing only the answer without extra details

dig +stats.translation_modifier: displaying query timing and server statistics
dig +stats.rationale: Shows additional diagnostic information; still read-only.

dig +tcp.translation_modifier: using TCP instead of UDP for the query
dig +tcp.rationale: Changes the transport protocol; still a read-only query.

dig +timeout.translation_modifier: setting a custom timeout for the query
dig +timeout.rationale: Changes how long to wait for a response; still a read-only query.

dig +trace.translation_modifier: tracing the full delegation path from root servers
dig +trace.rationale: Shows the complete DNS resolution path; still read-only.

dig -4.translation_modifier: using only IPv4 for the query
dig -4.rationale: Restricts the network protocol; still a read-only query.

dig -6.translation_modifier: using only IPv6 for the query
dig -6.rationale: Restricts the network protocol; still a read-only query.

dig -b.translation_modifier: sending the query from a specific local IP address
dig -b.rationale: Binds to a specific source address; still a read-only query.

dig -f.translation_modifier: reading a list of lookup requests from a file
dig -f.rationale: Batch mode for multiple queries; still read-only.

dig -p.translation_modifier: sending the query to a non-standard port
dig -p.rationale: Changes the destination port; still a read-only query.

dig -t.translation_modifier: querying for a specified record type
dig -t.rationale: Changes the DNS record type requested; still read-only.

dig -x.translation_modifier: performing a reverse lookup to find the hostname for an IP address

diskutil eject force.translation_modifier: forcibly closing any open files before ejecting
diskutil eject force.rationale: Forces ejection regardless of open files, which may cause data loss.

diskutil info -all.translation_modifier: showing information for every disk and partition
diskutil info -all.rationale: Widens the read-only query to all devices.

diskutil info -plist.rationale: Changes output to property list format; read-only.

diskutil list -plist.rationale: Changes output to property list format; read-only.

diskutil mergePartitions force.translation_modifier: reformatting the first partition as well
diskutil mergePartitions force.rationale: Destroys data on all partitions including the first, which is normally preserved.

diskutil mount -mountPoint.translation_modifier: at a custom mount location instead of the default
diskutil mount -mountPoint.rationale: Changes where the volume appears in the filesystem; does not affect data.

diskutil mount nobrowse.translation_modifier: hiding the volume from the Finder
diskutil mount nobrowse.rationale: Cosmetic change; the volume is still accessible.

diskutil mount readOnly.rationale: Prevents any modifications to the mounted volume.

diskutil unmount force.translation_modifier: forcibly closing any open files on the volume
diskutil unmount force.rationale: Forces unmount regardless of open files, which may cause data loss or corruption.

diskutil unmountDisk force.translation_modifier: forcibly closing any open files on all volumes
diskutil unmountDisk force.rationale: Forces unmount of all volumes regardless of open files, risking data loss.

diskutil zeroDisk force.rationale: Bypasses open-file checks, increasing the chance of data loss.

ditto --arch.translation_modifier: thinning universal binaries to only the specified architecture
ditto --arch.rationale: Removes other architectures from copied binaries; the destination copy will only run on the specified architecture.

ditto --bom.translation_modifier: copying only files listed in a bill of materials file
ditto --bom.rationale: Limits the copy to a specific file list; reduces scope.

ditto --clone.translation_modifier: attempting to clone files instead of copying their data
ditto --clone.rationale: Uses copy-on-write cloning for efficiency; data is preserved identically.

ditto --hfsCompression.translation_modifier: compressing files with filesystem-level compression at the destination
ditto --hfsCompression.rationale: Applies transparent compression; files remain fully readable.

ditto --keepParent.translation_modifier: embedding the parent directory name inside the archive
ditto --keepParent.rationale: Changes archive structure; does not affect source files.

ditto --noacl.rationale: Omits ACL data; copied files may have different permissions than the originals.

ditto --noextattr.rationale: Omits extended attributes; may lose metadata like quarantine flags.

ditto --noqtn.rationale: Removes the quarantine flag, allowing downloaded files to open without Gatekeeper warnings.

ditto --norsrc.translation_modifier: skipping resource forks, extended attributes, and access control lists
ditto --norsrc.rationale: Omits macOS-specific metadata from the copy; reduces what is transferred.

ditto --password.translation_modifier: prompting for a password to extract an encrypted ZIP archive

ditto --rsrc.translation_modifier: preserving resource forks and HFS metadata
ditto --rsrc.rationale: Ensures macOS-specific metadata is copied; does not change scope.

ditto --sequesterRsrc.translation_modifier: storing resource forks in a __MACOSX subdirectory inside the archive
ditto --sequesterRsrc.rationale: Changes how metadata is stored in ZIP archives; does not affect source files.

ditto -V.rationale: Prints a line for every file, link, and device copied; does not change copy behavior.

ditto -X.translation_modifier: without crossing filesystem boundaries into other volumes
ditto -X.rationale: Limits the copy scope by skipping directories on different volumes.

ditto -c.translation_modifier: creating an archive at the destination instead of copying files
ditto -c.rationale: Creates an archive; may overwrite an existing file at the destination.

ditto -j.translation_modifier: using bzip2 compression for the archive
ditto -j.rationale: Adds compression; does not change what is copied.

ditto -k.translation_modifier: using PKZip format instead of the default archive format
ditto -k.rationale: Changes the archive format; does not change what is copied.

ditto -v.rationale: Prints a line for each source directory copied; does not change copy behavior.

ditto -x.rationale: Extracts archive contents, potentially overwriting existing files at the destination.

ditto -z.translation_modifier: using gzip compression for the archive
ditto -z.rationale: Adds compression; does not change what is copied.

dmesg -M.translation_modifier: reading messages from a specific system memory image file
dmesg -M.rationale: Only changes the source of the log data; still a read-only operation.

dmesg -N.translation_modifier: using a specific kernel image to interpret the messages
dmesg -N.rationale: Only changes how messages are interpreted; still a read-only operation.

docker build --build-arg.translation_modifier: passing a build-time variable to the Dockerfile
docker build --build-arg.rationale: Build args may contain secrets that get baked into image layers if not handled carefully.

docker build --no-cache.translation_modifier: without using any cached layers from previous builds
docker build --no-cache.rationale: Forces a full rebuild; slower but ensures all layers are fresh.

docker build -f.translation_modifier: using a specific Dockerfile instead of the default
docker build -f.rationale: Allows building from an alternate Dockerfile; no additional risk beyond the chosen file's contents.

docker build -t.translation_modifier: tagging the resulting image with a name and optional version
docker build -t.rationale: Assigns a name to the built image; no additional risk.

docker compose down --remove-orphans.translation_modifier: also removing containers for services no longer defined in the Compose file
docker compose down --remove-orphans.rationale: Removes containers that may have been intentionally kept from a previous configuration.

docker compose down --rmi.translation_modifier: also removing images used by the services
docker compose down --rmi.rationale: Deletes service images which must be rebuilt or re-pulled to restart services.

docker compose down -v.translation_modifier: also deleting named volumes declared in the Compose file
docker compose down -v.rationale: Permanently removes volumes and their data, including databases and application state.

docker compose rm --force.rationale: Skips the confirmation prompt before removing containers.

docker compose rm -v.translation_modifier: also deleting anonymous volumes attached to the containers
docker compose rm -v.rationale: Permanently removes anonymous volumes and their data along with the containers.

docker compose run --rm.translation_modifier: automatically removing the container when it exits
docker compose run --rm.rationale: Cleans up the one-off container on exit; prevents orphaned containers.

docker compose up --build.rationale: Ensures images are up to date; adds build time but no additional risk.

docker compose up --force-recreate.translation_modifier: recreating containers even if their configuration has not changed
docker compose up --force-recreate.rationale: Destroys and recreates containers, which may cause brief downtime and loss of container state.

docker compose up -d.rationale: Runs services detached; they continue running after the command returns.

docker container prune --force.rationale: Skips the confirmation prompt before removing stopped containers.

docker exec --privileged.translation_modifier: with elevated privileges inside the container
docker exec --privileged.rationale: Grants the executed command extended kernel capabilities beyond the container's defaults.

docker exec -it.rationale: Allocates a terminal for interactive use; no additional risk beyond the base command.

docker exec -u.rationale: Running as root inside the container grants full control over the container's filesystem.

docker image prune --all.translation_modifier: including all unused images, not just dangling ones
docker image prune --all.rationale: Removes every image not referenced by a container, causing lengthy re-downloads.

docker image prune --force.rationale: Skips the confirmation prompt before deleting images.

docker kill -s.rationale: Different signals have different effects; some may cause data corruption if the process is not signal-safe.

docker logs --tail.translation_modifier: showing only the specified number of most recent lines
docker logs --tail.rationale: Limits output to recent lines; read-only operation.

docker logs -f.translation_modifier: streaming new log lines as they are produced
docker logs -f.rationale: Follows the log stream; still a read-only operation.

docker network prune --force.rationale: Skips the confirmation prompt, increasing the chance of accidental deletion.

docker ps -a.rationale: Shows all containers regardless of state; read-only operation.

docker pull --all-tags.translation_modifier: downloading every tagged version of the image
docker pull --all-tags.rationale: Can consume significant disk space and bandwidth by pulling all image variants.

docker push --all-tags.translation_modifier: uploading every tagged version of the image
docker push --all-tags.rationale: Publishes all local tags for the image, which may include experimental or unready versions.

docker rm --force.translation_modifier: killing and removing a running container
docker rm --force.rationale: Forcefully kills a running container before removing it, potentially causing data loss.

docker rm -v.translation_modifier: also deleting anonymous volumes attached to the container
docker rm -v.rationale: Permanently removes anonymous volumes and their data along with the container.

docker rmi --force.translation_modifier: even if the image is used by stopped containers
docker rmi --force.rationale: Forcefully removes a local image; the image can be re-pulled from the registry.

docker run --cap-add.translation_modifier: granting additional Linux kernel capabilities to the container
docker run --cap-add.rationale: Weakens container isolation by adding specific kernel privileges.

docker run --cap-drop.translation_modifier: removing Linux kernel capabilities from the container
docker run --cap-drop.rationale: Strengthens container isolation by dropping specific kernel privileges.

docker run --cpus.translation_modifier: limiting the number of CPU cores available to the container
docker run --cpus.rationale: Constrains resource usage; a protective measure that does not increase risk.

docker run --env.translation_modifier: setting an environment variable inside the container
docker run --env.rationale: Environment variables may contain secrets; they are visible in container inspection output.

docker run --memory.rationale: Constrains resource usage; a protective measure that does not increase risk.

docker run --name.translation_modifier: assigning a specific name to the container
docker run --name.rationale: Names the container for easier reference; no behavioral change.

docker run --network.translation_modifier: connecting the container to a specific network
docker run --network.rationale: Controls network isolation; using 'host' mode exposes all host ports to the container.

docker run --pid.translation_modifier: sharing process visibility with the host or another container
docker run --pid.rationale: Using 'host' mode allows the container to see and signal all host processes.

docker run --privileged.translation_modifier: with full access to the host system's devices and kernel capabilities
docker run --privileged.rationale: Grants the container nearly unrestricted host access, bypassing all security isolation.

docker run --read-only.translation_modifier: making the container's root filesystem read-only
docker run --read-only.rationale: Improves security by preventing writes to the container filesystem.

docker run --restart.translation_modifier: with a specific restart policy when the container exits
docker run --restart.rationale: Containers with 'always' or 'unless-stopped' policies restart automatically, which may persist unintended workloads.

docker run --rm.translation_modifier: automatically removing the container when it exits
docker run --rm.rationale: Cleans up the container on exit, preventing orphaned containers.

docker run -d.rationale: Runs the container detached; the container continues running after the command returns.

docker run -it.rationale: Allocates a terminal for interactive use; no additional risk beyond the base command.

docker run -p.translation_modifier: publishing a container port to the host
docker run -p.rationale: Exposes the container's service on the host network, making it accessible externally.

docker run -v.translation_modifier: mounting a host directory or volume into the container
docker run -v.rationale: Gives the container read/write access to host files, which could lead to data modification or exposure.

docker system prune --all.translation_modifier: including all unused images, not just dangling ones
docker system prune --all.rationale: Removes every unused image, causing lengthy re-downloads, but images are recoverable from registries.

docker system prune --force.rationale: Skips the confirmation prompt before a bulk-delete of multiple resource types.

docker system prune --volumes.translation_modifier: also deleting unused volumes and their data
docker system prune --volumes.rationale: Extends the prune to include volumes, permanently destroying persistent data.

docker volume prune --all.translation_modifier: including named volumes, not just anonymous ones
docker volume prune --all.rationale: Extends deletion to explicitly named volumes which often contain important persistent data.

docker volume prune --force.rationale: Skips the confirmation prompt before bulk-deleting volumes.

docker volume rm --force.translation_modifier: without raising an error if the volume does not exist
docker volume rm --force.rationale: Only suppresses 'not found' errors; does not add destructive capability beyond the base command.

docker-compose build --no-cache.translation_modifier: rebuilding from scratch without using any cached layers
docker-compose build --no-cache.rationale: Increases build time but produces a clean image; does not add destructive capability.

docker-compose down --dry-run.translation_modifier: simulating the operation without actually stopping or removing anything
docker-compose down --dry-run.rationale: No containers or networks are affected; only shows what would happen.

docker-compose down --remove-orphans.translation_modifier: also removing containers for services no longer in the Compose file
docker-compose down --remove-orphans.rationale: Deletes containers not in the current configuration.

docker-compose down --rmi.translation_modifier: also removing images used by the services
docker-compose down --rmi.rationale: Deletes images that can be re-pulled or rebuilt, but adds cleanup time.

docker-compose down -v.translation_modifier: also removing named and anonymous volumes
docker-compose down -v.rationale: Destroys persistent data stored in volumes, which may be irrecoverable.

docker-compose exec --privileged.rationale: Grants near-root access to the host system from within the container.

docker-compose exec -u.rationale: Changes the user context for the command but does not add destructive capability.

docker-compose kill -s.translation_modifier: using a specified signal instead of immediate termination signal
docker-compose kill -s.rationale: Allows choosing a different signal; does not increase destructive potential.

docker-compose rm --dry-run.translation_modifier: simulating the operation without actually removing anything
docker-compose rm --dry-run.rationale: No containers are removed; only shows what would happen.

docker-compose rm -f.rationale: Bypasses the confirmation prompt on container removal, which deletes container state.

docker-compose rm -s.translation_modifier: stopping the containers first if they are running
docker-compose rm -s.rationale: Stops running containers before removing them, interrupting active services.

docker-compose rm -v.translation_modifier: also removing anonymous volumes attached to the containers
docker-compose rm -v.rationale: Destroys anonymous volumes, permanently losing any data stored in them.

docker-compose run --dry-run.translation_modifier: simulating the operation without actually running anything
docker-compose run --dry-run.rationale: No container is created; only shows what would happen.

docker-compose run --no-deps.rationale: Reduces the scope of what is started; a safety measure.

docker-compose run --rm.translation_modifier: automatically removing the container when it exits
docker-compose run --rm.rationale: Cleans up the temporary container after use; prevents container accumulation.

docker-compose up --build.rationale: Triggers an image build; does not add destructive capability.

docker-compose up --dry-run.translation_modifier: simulating the operation without actually creating or starting anything
docker-compose up --dry-run.rationale: No containers are created or started; only shows what would happen.

docker-compose up --force-recreate.translation_modifier: recreating all containers even if unchanged
docker-compose up --force-recreate.rationale: Destroys and recreates containers, losing any ephemeral state inside them.

docker-compose up --remove-orphans.translation_modifier: removing containers for services no longer defined in the Compose file
docker-compose up --remove-orphans.rationale: Deletes containers that are not in the current configuration, which may still hold data.

docker-compose up -V.translation_modifier: recreating anonymous volumes instead of reusing data from previous containers
docker-compose up -V.rationale: Destroys and recreates anonymous volumes, permanently losing any data stored in them.

docker-compose up -d.rationale: Detaches from the terminal but does not change what is created or started.

dropdb --force.translation_modifier: forcibly disconnecting all active users before dropping the database
