watch -w.translation_modifier: wrapping long lines instead of truncating them
watch -w.rationale: Display formatting only; no effect on data.

watch -x.translation_modifier: passing the command to a shell for execution
watch -x.rationale: Uses shell interpretation instead of direct execution; the risk depends on the command itself, not this flag.

wc -L.translation_modifier: showing only the length of the longest line
wc -L.rationale: Reports the longest line length instead of standard counts; still read-only.

wc -c.rationale: Restricts output to byte counts; still read-only.

wc -l.rationale: Restricts output to line counts; still read-only.

wc -m.rationale: Restricts output to character counts, which may differ from byte counts for multibyte encodings; still read-only.

wc -w.rationale: Restricts output to word counts; still read-only.

wdutil diagnose -f.translation_modifier: saving the output to a specified directory instead of the default location
wdutil diagnose -f.rationale: Only changes where diagnostic files are written.

which -a.translation_modifier: listing all matching executables found in the PATH, not just the first
which -a.rationale: Expands the output to show all matches; still a read-only operation.

which -s.translation_modifier: producing no output and only returning an exit code
which -s.rationale: Suppresses output; returns 0 if found, 1 if not. Still read-only.

who -H.translation_modifier: including column headings in the output
who -H.rationale: Only changes output formatting; read-only operation.

who -T.translation_modifier: showing whether each user is accepting messages
who -T.rationale: Only adds message-status information to the output; read-only operation.

who -a.translation_modifier: including system boot time, idle time, and message status for all entries
who -a.rationale: Only adds more detail to the output; read-only operation.

who -b.translation_modifier: showing the time and date of the last system reboot
who -b.rationale: Only displays reboot information; read-only operation.

who -m.translation_modifier: showing only information about the current terminal
who -m.rationale: Only restricts which terminal is displayed; read-only operation.

who -q.translation_modifier: showing only login names and a count of logged-in users
who -q.rationale: Only changes the output format to a compact listing; read-only operation.

who -u.translation_modifier: showing idle time for each user
who -u.rationale: Only adds idle time information to the output; read-only operation.

whois -Q.translation_modifier: performing a quick lookup without following referrals
whois -Q.rationale: Limits the query to a single server; still read-only.

whois -R.translation_modifier: following referrals to other servers recursively
whois -R.rationale: Follows referrals for more complete results; still read-only.

whois -S.translation_modifier: showing raw, unfiltered output from the server

whois -a.translation_modifier: querying the American internet registry database
whois -a.rationale: Selects a specific regional database; still read-only.

whois -h.translation_modifier: querying a specified server instead of the default
whois -h.rationale: Redirects the query to a different server; still read-only.

whois -p.rationale: Changes the connection port; still a read-only query.

whois -r.translation_modifier: querying the European internet registry database
whois -r.rationale: Selects a specific regional database; still read-only.

xargs -0.translation_modifier: using null characters as input separators instead of spaces and newlines
xargs -0.rationale: Handles file names with spaces and special characters correctly; a robustness improvement.

xargs -I.translation_modifier: replacing a placeholder string with each input item
xargs -I.rationale: Changes how arguments are substituted into the command; does not add destructive capability.

xargs -J.translation_modifier: inserting all input arguments at a specified position in the command
xargs -J.rationale: Changes where arguments are placed in the command; does not add destructive capability.

xargs -L.translation_modifier: running the command once for every specified number of input lines
xargs -L.rationale: Controls how input is batched; does not change which command is executed.

xargs -P.translation_modifier: running multiple command invocations in parallel
xargs -P.rationale: Launches multiple processes at once, which increases resource usage and makes errors harder to trace.

xargs -n.translation_modifier: limiting each command invocation to a specified number of arguments
xargs -n.rationale: Controls how many arguments are passed per execution; does not change what command is run.

xargs -p.translation_modifier: prompting for confirmation before executing each command
xargs -p.rationale: Adds an interactive confirmation step before each execution; a safety improvement.

xargs -r.translation_modifier: skipping execution if the input is empty
xargs -r.rationale: Prevents running the command with no arguments; a safety improvement.

xargs -s.translation_modifier: limiting the total command line length to a specified number of bytes
xargs -s.rationale: Caps the size of each constructed command; does not change what is executed.

xargs -t.translation_modifier: printing each command to the screen before executing it
xargs -t.rationale: Shows what will be run for visibility; does not change behavior.

xattr -c.translation_modifier: clearing all extended attributes from the file
xattr -c.rationale: Removes all extended attributes at once, including security metadata; may bypass Gatekeeper protections.

xattr -d.rationale: Removes a single extended attribute; deleting security metadata like quarantine flags may bypass Gatekeeper.

xattr -l.translation_modifier: displaying both attribute names and their values
xattr -l.rationale: Read-only display of attribute names and values.

xattr -p.translation_modifier: printing the value of a specific named attribute
xattr -p.rationale: Read-only display of a single attribute value.

xattr -r.translation_modifier: recursively through all files in subdirectories
xattr -r.rationale: Widens the scope to an entire directory tree.

xattr -s.translation_modifier: acting on the symbolic link itself rather than its target
xattr -s.rationale: Changes which file is affected; does not widen scope.

xattr -v.rationale: Forces display of the file name even for a single file; cosmetic only.

xattr -w.translation_modifier: writing a value to a named attribute
xattr -w.rationale: Modifies or creates an extended attribute; may change security metadata or quarantine flags.

xattr -x.translation_modifier: displaying or accepting attribute values in hexadecimal format
xattr -x.rationale: Changes the display or input format; does not affect the attribute data itself.

xcode-select --install.translation_modifier: opening a dialog to install the command line developer tools
xcode-select --install.rationale: Downloads and installs developer tools, which modifies system files.

xcode-select --reset.translation_modifier: resetting the active developer directory to the default
xcode-select --reset.rationale: Changes the active Xcode toolchain; may affect builds that depend on a specific version.

xcode-select -p.translation_modifier: printing the path to the currently active developer directory
xcode-select -p.rationale: Read-only display of the current developer directory path.

xcode-select -s.translation_modifier: switching the active developer directory to a specified path
xcode-select -s.rationale: Changes which Xcode toolchain is used system-wide; may affect builds that depend on a specific version.

xcrun --find.translation_modifier: printing the path to a tool instead of running it
xcrun --find.rationale: Read-only lookup that displays the tool path without executing anything.

xcrun --kill-cache.translation_modifier: clearing the developer tool lookup cache
xcrun --kill-cache.rationale: Removes the cache; all values must be re-cached, which may slow the next lookup.

xcrun --log.rationale: Prints the full command line being invoked; does not change behavior.

xcrun --no-cache.translation_modifier: bypassing the cache for this lookup
xcrun --no-cache.rationale: Skips the cache for a single invocation; does not delete the cache.

xcrun --sdk.rationale: Limits the search to a named SDK; does not modify anything.

xcrun --show-sdk-build-version.translation_modifier: printing the build version of the selected SDK
xcrun --show-sdk-build-version.rationale: Read-only display of the SDK build version.

xcrun --show-sdk-path.translation_modifier: printing the path to the selected SDK
xcrun --show-sdk-path.rationale: Read-only display of the SDK path.

xcrun --show-sdk-platform-path.translation_modifier: printing the path to the platform for the selected SDK
xcrun --show-sdk-platform-path.rationale: Read-only display of the platform path.

xcrun --show-sdk-version.translation_modifier: printing the version number of the selected SDK
xcrun --show-sdk-version.rationale: Read-only display of the SDK version.

xcrun --toolchain.rationale: Limits the search to a named toolchain; does not modify anything.

xcrun -v.rationale: Adds verbose output about tool lookup; does not change behavior.

xgettext --force.rationale: Bypasses the overwrite prompt, silently replacing existing output files.

xsanctl --force.translation_modifier: forcing the operation without safety checks
xsanctl --force.rationale: Bypasses safety checks on storage area network operations; may cause data loss on shared storage.

xxd -a.translation_modifier: replacing identical lines with a single asterisk
xxd -a.rationale: Only compresses repeated output lines; no data change.

xxd -b.translation_modifier: showing binary digits instead of hexadecimal
xxd -b.rationale: Only changes the output format to binary representation.

xxd -c.translation_modifier: displaying a specified number of bytes per line
xxd -c.rationale: Only changes the column width of the output.

xxd -e.translation_modifier: displaying bytes in little-endian byte order
xxd -e.rationale: Only changes the byte order shown in the output.

xxd -g.translation_modifier: grouping bytes with a specified number of bytes per group
xxd -g.rationale: Only changes whitespace grouping in the output.

xxd -i.translation_modifier: producing output as a C source code array
xxd -i.rationale: Only changes the output format to a C include style.

xxd -l.translation_modifier: limiting output to a specified number of bytes
xxd -l.rationale: Only restricts how much of the file is displayed.

xxd -p.translation_modifier: using plain continuous hex dump format without line numbers or ASCII

xxd -r.translation_modifier: converting a hex dump back into binary data
xxd -r.rationale: Creates or overwrites binary output from hex input, which can modify files on disk.

xxd -s.translation_modifier: starting at a specified byte offset
xxd -s.rationale: Only changes the starting position for the hex dump.

xxd -u.translation_modifier: using uppercase letters for hex digits
xxd -u.rationale: Only changes the letter case in the output.

xz --force.translation_modifier: overwriting existing output files without prompting
xz --force.rationale: Overwrites existing output files without confirmation; recoverable from backups.

xz -d.rationale: Decompresses .xz files in place, replacing them with the original content.

xz -f.rationale: Forces operation even if the output file already exists.

xz -k.translation_modifier: keeping the original file instead of replacing it
xz -k.rationale: Preserves the source file; a safety-enhancing option.

xz -l.translation_modifier: listing compression information without modifying files

xz -t.translation_modifier: testing the integrity of compressed files without decompressing
xz -t.rationale: Read-only operation that verifies compressed file integrity without decompressing or modifying the file.

xzcat --force.translation_modifier: overwriting existing output files without prompting
xzcat --force.rationale: Overwrites existing output files without confirmation; recoverable from backups.

yarn add --dev.rationale: Changes the dependency category but does not alter the installation behavior.

yarn cache clean --all.translation_modifier: removing the entire cache including mirror files
yarn cache clean --all.rationale: Deletes all cached data, which may significantly slow down the next install.

yarn install --frozen-lockfile.translation_modifier: failing if the lockfile would need to be updated
yarn install --frozen-lockfile.rationale: Prevents lockfile changes; a safety check for CI environments in Yarn v1.

yarn install --immutable.translation_modifier: failing if the lockfile would need to be updated
yarn install --immutable.rationale: Prevents lockfile changes; a safety check for CI environments.

yarn upgrade --latest.translation_modifier: ignoring the version ranges in package.json and upgrading to the absolute latest versions
yarn upgrade --latest.rationale: May introduce major-version breaking changes by bypassing semver range constraints.

yarnpkg --all.translation_modifier: applying the operation to all workspaces
yarnpkg --all.rationale: Widens scope to every workspace in the project.

yarnpkg --force.translation_modifier: refetching all packages even if already downloaded
yarnpkg --force.rationale: Forces re-download of all packages, bypassing cache.

yarnpkg --reset.translation_modifier: resetting the lockfile and regenerating it from scratch
yarnpkg --reset.rationale: Deletes and recreates the lockfile; may change resolved dependency versions.

zcat --force.translation_modifier: overwriting existing output files without prompting
zcat --force.rationale: Overwrites existing output files without confirmation; recoverable from backups.

zcat --recursive.translation_modifier: recursively through all files in subdirectories
zcat --recursive.rationale: Processes entire directory trees, increasing the scope of files affected.

zip -9.rationale: Changes compression level only; does not affect which files are processed.

zip -@.translation_modifier: reading the list of files to archive from standard input
zip -@.rationale: Changes how input files are specified; does not add destructive capability.

zip -FS.translation_modifier: synchronizing the archive with the file system, removing entries that no longer exist on disk
zip -FS.rationale: Deletes archive entries that have no matching file on disk, which may cause unexpected data loss from the archive.

zip -T.translation_modifier: testing the archive integrity after creation
zip -T.rationale: Read-only validation of the archive; does not modify any files.

zip -d.translation_modifier: deleting specified entries from the archive
zip -d.rationale: Removes entries from an existing archive file.

zip -e.translation_modifier: encrypting the archive with a password
zip -e.rationale: Adds password protection; does not change the archive contents.

zip -f.translation_modifier: freshening the archive by replacing only entries that already exist and are newer
zip -f.rationale: Only updates existing archive entries; does not add new files or modify source files.

zip -j.translation_modifier: storing files without their directory paths
zip -j.rationale: Flattens the directory structure in the archive; source files are not modified.

zip -m.translation_modifier: deleting the original files after adding them to the archive
zip -m.rationale: Removes source files after archiving; data is only in the zip file.

zip -q.rationale: Suppresses output messages; does not change behavior.

zip -r.translation_modifier: recursively including all files in subdirectories
zip -r.rationale: Includes directory trees in the archive; source files are not modified.

zip -u.translation_modifier: updating only files that are newer than those already in the archive
zip -u.rationale: Only replaces archive entries with newer versions; source files are not modified.

zip -x.translation_modifier: excluding files that match specified patterns
zip -x.rationale: Reduces the set of files added to the archive; source files are not affected.

zstd --long.translation_modifier: using a larger search window for better compression of files with distant repeated patterns
zstd --long.rationale: Increases memory usage for better compression; does not change which files are processed.

zstd --rm.translation_modifier: removing the source file after successful compression or decompression
zstd --rm.rationale: Deletes the input file, leaving only the output.

zstd --ultra.translation_modifier: enabling ultra-high compression levels that use significantly more memory
zstd --ultra.rationale: Unlocks higher compression levels; does not change which files are processed.

zstd -19.rationale: Changes compression level only; does not affect which files are processed.

zstd -C.translation_modifier: adding an integrity checksum to verify data has not been corrupted
zstd -C.rationale: Adds a verification checksum; does not change the data.

zstd -T0.translation_modifier: using all available processor cores for compression
zstd -T0.rationale: Increases compression speed through parallelism; does not change which files are processed.

zstd -c.translation_modifier: writing output to standard output and keeping the original file
zstd -c.rationale: Leaves the original file intact; output goes to standard output.

zstd -d.rationale: Decompresses .zst files, creating or replacing the original file.

zstd -f.rationale: Forces operation even if the output file already exists.

zstd -k.translation_modifier: keeping the source file after compression or decompression
zstd -k.rationale: Preserves the input file; this is the default behavior.

zstd -l.translation_modifier: listing compression information without modifying files

zstd -r.rationale: Processes all files in a directory tree.

zstd -t.translation_modifier: testing the integrity of compressed files without decompressing
zstd -t.rationale: Read-only operation that verifies compressed file integrity.

zstdcat --force.translation_modifier: overwriting existing output files without prompting
zstdcat --force.rationale: Overwrites existing output files without confirmation; recoverable from backups.

zstdmt --force.translation_modifier: overwriting existing output files without prompting
zstdmt --force.rationale: Overwrites existing output files without confirmation; recoverable from backups.

aws ec2 run-instances --dry-run.translation: Simulate launching EC2 instances to validate permissions and parameters without actually creating any resources.
aws ec2 run-instances --dry-run.rationale: No instances are created; only checks whether the caller has the required permissions and the parameters are valid.

aws rds delete-db-instance --skip-final-.translation: Delete an RDS database instance without creating a final backup snapshot, permanently destroying all data.
aws rds delete-db-instance --skip-final-.rationale: Bypasses the default final snapshot, making all database data permanently irrecoverable after deletion.

aws s3 cp --recursive.translation: Copy an entire directory tree between the local filesystem and S3, or between S3 locations, overwriting any existing objects at the destination.
aws s3 cp --recursive.rationale: Transfers a full directory tree that may silently overwrite existing data at the destination.

aws s3 rb --force.translation: Empty an S3 bucket by deleting all its objects and then permanently destroy the bucket itself.
aws s3 rb --force.rationale: Irreversibly removes both the data and the bucket; the bucket name may not be immediately reusable.

aws s3 rm --dryrun --recursive.translation: Simulate recursively deleting all objects under an S3 prefix without actually removing anything.
aws s3 rm --dryrun --recursive.rationale: No objects are deleted; only displays what would be removed, allowing safe review before execution.

aws s3 rm --recursive.translation: Delete all objects under a specified S3 prefix, potentially wiping the entire contents of a bucket.
aws s3 rm --recursive.rationale: Recursively removes every object matching the prefix with no confirmation prompt; recovery depends on versioning.

aws s3 sync --delete.translation: Synchronize a local directory and an S3 prefix, deleting any files in the destination that do not exist in the source.
aws s3 sync --delete.rationale: Removes destination objects not present in the source, which can cause permanent data loss alongside the sync.

bash -c.translation: Execute a command string passed as an argument in a new Bash shell process.
bash -c.rationale: Runs an inline command in a subshell; the risk depends entirely on the command being executed.

bash -e.translation: Run a Bash shell that exits immediately if any command returns a non-zero status.
bash -e.rationale: Adds strict error handling that stops execution on failure, reducing the chance of cascading errors.

bash -x.translation: Run a Bash shell that prints each command to standard error before executing it.
bash -x.rationale: Adds debug tracing for visibility into what commands are running; does not change what is executed.

black --check.translation: Check whether Python source files need formatting without modifying them.
black --check.rationale: Read-only validation commonly used in CI pipelines to enforce consistent formatting.

black --check --diff.translation: Check whether Python source files need formatting and show the exact changes that would be made, without modifying any files.
black --check --diff.rationale: Combines format checking with a diff preview, providing full visibility into what black would change.

brew cleanup --prune.translation: Remove old formula versions and delete all cached downloads older than the specified number of days from disk.
brew cleanup --prune.rationale: Aggressively prunes the download cache based on age, which may force large re-downloads on the next install or upgrade.

brew install --cask.translation: Download and install a macOS desktop application from the Homebrew cask repository.
brew install --cask.rationale: Installs a graphical application that may register system-wide integrations, launch agents, or require elevated permissions.

brew uninstall --force.translation: Remove all installed versions of a formula and ignore dependency checks, which may break other installed software.
brew uninstall --force.rationale: Skips dependency verification and removes every version at once, potentially leaving other formulas with missing dependencies.

brew upgrade --greedy.translation: Upgrade all installed formulas and casks to their latest versions, including casks that normally auto-update themselves.
brew upgrade --greedy.rationale: Expands the upgrade to include auto-updating casks, which may introduce unexpected version changes in applications that manage their own updates.

cargo build --release.translation: Compile the current Rust package with full optimizations enabled, producing a production-ready binary.
cargo build --release.rationale: Produces an optimized binary locally; takes longer than a debug build but does not change what is modified.

cargo install --force.translation: Download, compile, and install a Rust binary from the registry, overwriting any existing installation of the same package.
cargo install --force.rationale: Forces replacement of an already-installed binary without confirmation, which may disrupt tools that depend on the current version.

cargo publish --allow-dirty.translation: Upload the current package to a Rust registry even though the working directory contains uncommitted changes.
cargo publish --allow-dirty.rationale: Publishes code that may include unintended local modifications because the clean-working-directory check is bypassed.

cargo publish --dry-run.translation: Simulate uploading the current package to a Rust registry, running validation checks without actually publishing.
cargo publish --dry-run.rationale: No package is uploaded; only performs build verification and metadata checks.

cargo run --release.translation: Compile the current Rust package with full optimizations and immediately execute the resulting binary.
cargo run --release.rationale: Runs the program in release mode; the optimization level changes but the program's behavior and capabilities remain the same.

cargo test --no-fail-fast.translation: Run all tests for the current Rust package, continuing to execute remaining tests even after a failure is encountered.
cargo test --no-fail-fast.rationale: Runs the complete test suite regardless of failures, which is useful for getting a full picture of test health.

cargo test --workspace.translation: Run the tests for every package in the Rust workspace.
cargo test --workspace.rationale: Extends testing to all workspace members; still a local compilation and execution operation.

chmod -L -R.translation: Change permissions recursively through all subdirectories, following symbolic links to reach files outside the directory tree.
chmod -L -R.rationale: Permission changes can propagate beyond the intended directory tree by following symbolic links.

chmod -R.translation: Change permissions on an entire directory tree and all files within it.
chmod -R.rationale: Applies permission changes recursively, which can expose or lock out access to large numbers of files at once.

chmod -R -v.translation: Change permissions on an entire directory tree, showing each file as its permissions are changed.
chmod -R -v.rationale: Applies recursive permission changes with verbose output for visibility into what is being modified.

cp -a.translation: Copy an entire directory tree to a new location, preserving all file attributes, permissions, and symbolic links.
cp -a.rationale: Creates a faithful mirror of a directory tree with full metadata preservation; source is unchanged.

cp -f.translation: Copy files to a new location, forcefully removing and recreating destination files that cannot be overwritten.
cp -f.rationale: Bypasses permission restrictions at the destination by deleting and recreating files, but the source is unchanged.

cp -p -r.translation: Copy an entire directory and all its contents to a new location, preserving file timestamps, permissions, and ownership.
cp -p -r.rationale: Duplicates a directory tree with metadata preservation; source is unchanged.

cp -r.translation: Copy an entire directory and all its contents to a new location.
cp -r.rationale: Duplicates a directory tree, potentially overwriting files at the destination but leaving the source unchanged.

curl -H -X -d.translation: Send an HTTP request with a custom method, headers, and a data payload to a remote server.
curl -H -X -d.rationale: Composes a full API request that transmits arbitrary data to a remote endpoint, commonly used for POST/PUT operations.

curl -I.translation: Fetch only the HTTP response headers from a remote server without downloading the body.
curl -I.rationale: Performs a HEAD request to a remote server, which still establishes a network connection but transfers minimal data.

curl -L -o.translation: Download a file from a server, following any redirects, and save it to a specified local path.
curl -L -o.rationale: Follows redirects and writes the final response to disk, which could overwrite local files with content from an unexpected host.

curl -k -L.translation: Transfer data from a server, following redirects and skipping TLS certificate verification.
curl -k -L.rationale: Combines redirect-following with disabled certificate checks, allowing connections to untrusted servers across the redirect chain.

curl -s.translation: Transfer data to or from a server silently, without showing progress or error output.
curl -s.rationale: Performs a network request with suppressed output, commonly used in scripts where errors may go unnoticed.

docker build --no-cache -t.translation: Build a container image from scratch without using cached layers, tagging the result with a specific name and optional version.
docker build --no-cache -t.rationale: Forces a complete rebuild and tags it; slower but guarantees all layers are freshly built.

docker container prune --force.translation: Remove all stopped containers without asking for confirmation.
docker container prune --force.rationale: Deletes all stopped containers immediately; writable layer data not stored in volumes is lost.

docker exec -it.translation: Open an interactive terminal session inside a running container.
docker exec -it.rationale: Standard pattern for interactive debugging or administration inside a running container.

docker image prune --all --force.translation: Remove all unused container images without asking for confirmation, not just dangling ones.
docker image prune --all --force.rationale: Deletes every image not referenced by a running container without prompting, requiring lengthy re-downloads to restore them.

docker network prune --force.translation: Remove all unused Docker networks without asking for confirmation.
docker network prune --force.rationale: Deletes unused networks immediately; they can be recreated but services may need reconfiguration.

docker rm --force.translation: Kill and remove a running container immediately, discarding any in-progress work without graceful shutdown.
docker rm --force.rationale: Forcefully terminates and removes a running container, potentially causing data corruption in applications that need graceful shutdown.

docker rm --force -v.translation: Kill and remove a running container immediately, also permanently deleting its anonymous volumes and their data.
docker rm --force -v.rationale: Combines forced container termination with anonymous volume deletion, permanently destroying both the container and its associated data.

docker rmi --force.translation: Forcefully remove a local container image even if stopped containers still reference it.
docker rmi --force.rationale: Removes the image regardless of stopped container references; the image can be re-pulled from the registry.

docker run --privileged.translation: Create and start a new container with full access to the host system's devices and kernel capabilities, bypassing all Docker security isolation.
docker run --privileged.rationale: Grants the container nearly unrestricted host access, equivalent to running processes directly on the host.

docker run --privileged -v.translation: Create and start a new container with full host access and a mounted host directory, giving the container unrestricted read/write access to host files and kernel.
docker run --privileged -v.rationale: Combines full kernel access with host filesystem mounts, enabling complete control over the host system from inside the container.

docker run -d.translation: Create and start a new container in the background, returning control immediately while the container continues running.
docker run -d.rationale: Standard pattern for running services; the container persists until explicitly stopped.

docker run -it --rm.translation: Create and start a new container with an interactive terminal attached, automatically removing the container when it exits.
docker run -it --rm.rationale: Standard pattern for interactive one-off containers that clean up after themselves.

docker system prune --all --force.translation: Remove all unused containers, networks, and images without asking for confirmation, forcing re-downloads of any images needed later.
docker system prune --all --force.rationale: Bulk-deletes all unused Docker resources immediately with no confirmation prompt, potentially causing lengthy image re-downloads.

docker system prune --all --force --volu.translation: Remove all unused containers, networks, images, and volumes without asking for confirmation, permanently destroying any persistent data in unused volumes.
docker system prune --all --force --volu.rationale: The most destructive single Docker command — bulk-deletes everything unused including persistent volume data with no confirmation prompt.

docker volume prune --force.translation: Remove all unused Docker volumes and their data without asking for confirmation.
docker volume prune --force.rationale: Permanently destroys data in all unused volumes with no confirmation prompt, making recovery impossible.

docker-compose build --no-cache.translation: Rebuild all service images from scratch without using any cached layers from previous builds.
docker-compose build --no-cache.rationale: Produces clean images by ignoring the build cache, which increases build time but ensures no stale layers are reused.

docker-compose down --rmi -v.translation: Stop and remove all containers, networks, volumes, and images defined in the Compose file, permanently destroying persisted data and built images.
docker-compose down --rmi -v.rationale: Performs a complete teardown including images and volumes, requiring a full rebuild and causing irrecoverable data loss from volumes.

docker-compose down -v.translation: Stop and remove all containers, networks, and volumes defined in the Compose file, permanently destroying any persisted data.
docker-compose down -v.rationale: Combines full teardown with volume removal, irrecoverably deleting any data stored in named or anonymous volumes.

docker-compose rm -f -v.translation: Remove stopped service containers and their anonymous volumes without asking for confirmation, permanently losing any data stored in those volumes.
docker-compose rm -f -v.rationale: Bypasses the confirmation prompt while also destroying anonymous volume data, combining a safety override with irrecoverable data loss.

docker-compose up --build -d.translation: Rebuild all service images and then start the containers in the background.
docker-compose up --build -d.rationale: Ensures containers run the latest code by rebuilding before launching in detached mode.

eslint --ext --fix.translation: Analyze files with specified extensions and automatically fix all problems that have safe corrections.
eslint --ext --fix.rationale: Combines extension filtering with auto-fix, limiting which files are modified to those matching the specified extensions.

eslint --fix.translation: Analyze JavaScript and TypeScript code and automatically fix all problems that have safe corrections.
eslint --fix.rationale: Modifies source files in place but only applies well-defined auto-fix rules that are considered safe by the ESLint community.

eslint --format.translation: Analyze JavaScript and TypeScript code and output the results using a specified formatter such as JSON or stylish.
eslint --format.rationale: Read-only analysis with customized output formatting, commonly used for CI integrations.

find -delete -empty.translation: Find all empty files and directories and permanently delete them.
find -delete -empty.rationale: Silently removes every empty file and directory under the search path with no confirmation or recovery.

find -delete -mtime.translation: Find files by their last modification time and permanently delete every match.
find -delete -mtime.rationale: Combines a time-based filter with immediate deletion, which can silently remove large numbers of files based on age.

find -delete -name.translation: Search for files matching a name pattern and permanently delete every match from disk.
find -delete -name.rationale: Combines a filename filter with immediate deletion, permanently removing all matching files with no recovery path.

find -delete -name -type.translation: Search for entries matching a name pattern and file type, then permanently delete every match.
find -delete -name -type.rationale: Targets files precisely by name and type before deleting, but still permanently removes all matches with no recovery.

find -exec -name.translation: Search for files matching a name pattern and run a specified command on each match.
find -exec -name.rationale: The risk depends entirely on the command passed to -exec; the find portion is a read-only filter.

find -name -type.translation: Search for files or directories matching a name pattern and restricted to a specific file type such as regular file or directory.
find -name -type.rationale: Combines two read-only filters to narrow search results precisely.

find -regex -type.translation: Search for files or directories whose full path matches a regular expression, restricted to a specific file type.
find -regex -type.rationale: Combines two read-only filters using regex for flexible path matching.

gcloud compute instances delete --delete.translation: Delete a Compute Engine instance along with its attached disks, permanently destroying all data stored on them.
gcloud compute instances delete --delete.rationale: Combines instance termination with disk deletion, making data recovery impossible.

gcloud compute instances delete --keep-d.translation: Delete a Compute Engine instance but preserve its attached disks for reuse or data recovery.
gcloud compute instances delete --keep-d.rationale: Terminates the instance but retains disk data, reducing data loss risk.

gcloud run deploy --allow-unauthenticate.translation: Deploy a Cloud Run service and make it publicly accessible without any authentication requirement.
gcloud run deploy --allow-unauthenticate.rationale: Exposes a live service to the public internet with no access controls, increasing the attack surface.

gcloud storage rm --all-versions --recur.translation: Recursively delete all objects and all historical versions under a Cloud Storage path, making recovery impossible even with versioning.
gcloud storage rm --all-versions --recur.rationale: Destroys both current objects and their version history, eliminating any versioning-based recovery path.

gcloud storage rm --recursive.translation: Recursively delete all objects under a Cloud Storage path, potentially wiping the entire contents of a bucket.
gcloud storage rm --recursive.rationale: Removes all objects matching the path prefix with no undo; recovery depends on object versioning being enabled.

gh api --method.translation: Make an authenticated request to the GitHub API using a specific HTTP method, which may create, modify, or delete remote resources.
gh api --method.rationale: Non-GET methods can mutate any resource the authenticated user has access to; the exact impact depends on the endpoint.

gh auth login.translation: Log in to a GitHub account, storing authentication credentials on the local machine.
gh auth login.rationale: Writes credentials locally; does not modify any remote GitHub resources.

gh auth logout.translation: Log out of a GitHub account, removing stored authentication credentials from the local machine.
gh auth logout.rationale: Deletes local credentials, which may disrupt automated workflows but is trivially reversible by logging in again.

gh issue close.translation: Close an issue on GitHub, marking it as resolved without deleting it.
gh issue close.rationale: Changes the issue state to closed; can be reopened at any time.

gh issue create.translation: Create a new issue on GitHub, visible to repository collaborators or the public depending on repository visibility.
gh issue create.rationale: Publishes an issue that can be closed or deleted afterward; no destructive impact.

gh pr checkout.translation: Fetch a pull request's branch from GitHub and check it out locally for testing or review.
gh pr checkout.rationale: Downloads the branch and switches the local working tree; the remote repository is not modified.

gh pr create.translation: Create a new pull request on GitHub, publishing it to repository collaborators for review.
gh pr create.rationale: Opens a new PR visible to collaborators; can be closed or deleted afterward.

gh pr create --draft.translation: Create a new pull request on GitHub in draft mode, signaling it is not ready for review or merging.
gh pr create --draft.rationale: Draft PRs cannot be merged until marked ready, reducing the risk of premature integration.

gh pr merge --delete-branch --squash.translation: Squash all commits into one and merge the pull request, then delete the source branch from both local and remote.
gh pr merge --delete-branch --squash.rationale: Permanently integrates code into the base branch and removes the source branch, which cannot be undone without force-pushing.

gh pr merge --merge.translation: Merge the pull request into the base branch using a merge commit that preserves all individual commits.
gh pr merge --merge.rationale: Integrates changes into the shared base branch, modifying the repository history visible to all collaborators.

gh pr merge --rebase.translation: Rebase the pull request's commits onto the base branch and merge them without a merge commit.
gh pr merge --rebase.rationale: Rewrites commit hashes during rebase, permanently altering the repository history on the base branch.

gh pr review --approve.translation: Approve a pull request, signaling it meets review requirements and may be eligible for merging.
gh pr review --approve.rationale: Posts an approval review that may satisfy branch protection rules and trigger auto-merge if configured.

gh release create --draft.translation: Create a new release on GitHub saved as a draft, invisible to the public until explicitly published.
gh release create --draft.rationale: Draft releases are not visible to users and can be edited or deleted before publishing.

gh release delete --cleanup-tag --yes.translation: Permanently delete a release and its associated Git tag without asking for confirmation.
gh release delete --cleanup-tag --yes.rationale: Destroys both the release and the tag in one step with no confirmation prompt, breaking references and automation.

gh repo clone.translation: Download a GitHub repository to the local machine, creating a new directory with a full copy of the code and history.
gh repo clone.rationale: Read-only fetch from remote that creates a local directory; the remote repository is not modified.

gh repo delete.translation: Permanently delete a GitHub repository, destroying all code, issues, pull requests, releases, and settings.
gh repo delete.rationale: Irrecoverable destruction of an entire repository and all its associated data.

gh repo fork.translation: Create a personal copy of someone else's repository on GitHub under your account.
gh repo fork.rationale: Creates a new remote repository; the source repository is not modified.

gh run watch.translation: Stream the live output of a GitHub Actions workflow run until it completes.
gh run watch.rationale: Read-only monitoring that does not affect the workflow's execution or results.

gh secret set.translation: Create or update a repository or organization secret used by GitHub Actions workflows.
gh secret set.rationale: Writes a sensitive value that workflows consume; an incorrect value could break deployments or leak credentials.

git add --all.translation: Stage every change in the entire working tree — new files, modifications, and deletions.
git add --all.rationale: May unintentionally stage files the user did not mean to include, such as secrets or build artifacts, but only affects the staging area.

git checkout --force.translation: Switch branches or restore files, discarding all uncommitted local changes without warning.
git checkout --force.rationale: Permanently throws away uncommitted work in the working tree without confirmation.

git clean -d -f.translation: Permanently delete all untracked files and directories from the working directory.
git clean -d -f.rationale: Extends deletion to entire untracked directory trees, increasing the scope of irrecoverable data loss.

git clean -f.translation: Permanently delete all untracked files from the working directory.
git clean -f.rationale: Untracked files are not stored in Git history and cannot be recovered once deleted.

git push --dry-run.translation: Simulate uploading local commits to a remote repository without actually sending any data.
git push --dry-run.rationale: No data is transmitted; only shows what would happen.

git push --force.translation: Force-upload local commits to a remote repository, overwriting its history even if other contributors have pushed since.
git push --force.rationale: Rewrites the remote branch's commit history, which can permanently discard other contributors' work.

git push --force --no-verify.translation: Force-upload local commits to a remote repository, overwriting its history and skipping all pre-push hooks.
git push --force --no-verify.rationale: Combines history rewriting with hook bypass, removing both the remote safety net and local pre-push checks.

git push --force-with-lease.translation: Upload local commits to a remote repository, overwriting its history only if no one else has pushed since your last fetch.
git push --force-with-lease.rationale: Safer than --force but still rewrites remote history; fails if the remote has diverged since your last fetch.

git reset --hard.translation: Discard all uncommitted changes and move the current branch to a specified commit, permanently erasing staged and working-directory modifications.
git reset --hard.rationale: Permanently deletes uncommitted work with no built-in recovery mechanism.

git reset --soft.translation: Move the current branch pointer to a specified commit while keeping all changes staged for a new commit.
git reset --soft.rationale: Only moves the branch pointer; all file contents remain intact in the staging area.

git rm --force.translation: Remove files from both the working directory and the repository index, even if they have uncommitted changes.
git rm --force.rationale: Deletes files with unstaged or staged modifications that may not be recoverable from Git history.

git stash drop.translation: Permanently delete a stash entry, discarding the saved changes with no way to recover them.
git stash drop.rationale: The stash entry is permanently removed; recovery is only possible via reflog before garbage collection.

go build -o.translation: Compile Go packages and their dependencies, writing the resulting executable to a specific output file.
go build -o.rationale: Compiles locally and places the binary at a user-specified path; does not execute anything.

go build -race.translation: Compile Go packages with the data race detector enabled, adding runtime instrumentation to detect concurrent access bugs.
go build -race.rationale: Builds locally with additional instrumentation; the binary is larger and slower but detects race conditions at runtime.

go clean -cache.translation: Delete the entire Go build cache, forcing all packages to be recompiled on the next build.
go clean -cache.rationale: Removes all cached compilation artifacts; they will be rebuilt automatically but the next build will be slower.

go get -u.translation: Download the latest versions of Go modules and their dependencies, updating go.mod and go.sum to match.
go get -u.rationale: Fetches newer versions of all dependencies from the internet, which may introduce breaking changes or unexpected behavior.

go test -cover.translation: Run the tests for Go packages while measuring and reporting code coverage percentages.
go test -cover.rationale: Adds coverage instrumentation to the test run; does not change test behavior or modify source files.

go test -race.translation: Run the tests for Go packages with the data race detector enabled, reporting any concurrent access violations.
go test -race.rationale: Adds runtime instrumentation to detect race conditions during test execution; does not change test logic.

go test -race -v.translation: Run the tests for Go packages with verbose output and the data race detector enabled, printing each test name and result.
go test -race -v.rationale: Combines verbose test output with race detection instrumentation; useful for debugging concurrency issues in test suites.

grep --include -n -r.translation: Recursively search only files whose names match a specified pattern, showing file names and line numbers for each match.
grep --include -n -r.rationale: Narrows recursive search to specific file types, reducing noise while remaining entirely read-only.

grep -c.translation: Count the number of lines matching a pattern in each file instead of displaying the matching lines.
grep -c.rationale: Produces a numeric summary rather than full output; entirely read-only.

grep -l -r.translation: Recursively search all files in subdirectories and list only the names of files that contain a match.
grep -l -r.rationale: Identifies which files contain a pattern across a directory tree without showing individual lines; entirely read-only.

grep -n -r.translation: Recursively search all files in subdirectories for lines matching a pattern, showing the file name and line number for each match.
grep -n -r.rationale: Combines recursive traversal with line numbers for efficient codebase-wide searching; entirely read-only.

grep -v.translation: Search file contents and show only the lines that do not match the given pattern.
grep -v.rationale: Inverts the match to display non-matching lines; entirely read-only.

jest --coverage --verbose.translation: Run all tests with detailed per-test results and collect code coverage statistics.
jest --coverage --verbose.rationale: Comprehensive test run with full visibility into individual results and coverage metrics.

jest --watch.translation: Run tests related to changed files and continuously re-run them whenever source files change.
jest --watch.rationale: Long-lived development mode that provides fast feedback on code changes.

jq -e.translation: Process JSON data and set the exit code to indicate whether the result is null or false, for use in conditional scripts.
jq -e.rationale: Adds exit-code signaling to the read-only JSON filter, enabling shell-level branching on query results.

jq -r.translation: Process JSON data and output string values without surrounding quotes or JSON formatting.
jq -r.rationale: Strips JSON quoting from string output, commonly used to extract plain-text values for use in shell pipelines.

jq -s.translation: Read all JSON inputs into a single array, then process the combined data as one unit.
jq -s.rationale: Collects multiple JSON values into one array before filtering, useful for cross-document aggregation.

kill -9.translation: Immediately and forcefully terminate a process with no opportunity for it to save data, release resources, or clean up.
kill -9.rationale: Sends an uncatchable signal that instantly kills the process, potentially causing data corruption or resource leaks.

kill -HUP.translation: Ask a process to reload its configuration files or shut down gracefully.
kill -HUP.rationale: Commonly used to trigger configuration reloads in daemons; most programs handle this signal gracefully.

kill -TERM.translation: Request a process to shut down gracefully, giving it a chance to save data and release resources.
kill -TERM.rationale: Sends the default termination signal, which most programs handle by performing an orderly shutdown.

kubectl apply --dry-run.translation: Validate a configuration file against the cluster without actually creating or modifying any resources.
kubectl apply --dry-run.rationale: No cluster resources are changed; only validates the configuration and shows what would happen.

kubectl apply --force.translation: Create or update Kubernetes resources by deleting and recreating any resource that cannot be patched in place.
kubectl apply --force.rationale: Destroys and recreates resources that resist patching, causing downtime and potential data loss for stateful workloads.

kubectl delete --all.translation: Delete every resource of the specified type in the current namespace, destroying all matching pods, services, or other objects at once.
kubectl delete --all.rationale: Removes all resources of a type in one operation, which can destroy an entire application or environment.

kubectl delete --all --all-namespaces.translation: Delete every resource of the specified type across all namespaces in the cluster, wiping matching objects cluster-wide.
kubectl delete --all --all-namespaces.rationale: Cluster-wide deletion of all resources of a type can destroy production workloads across every environment simultaneously.

kubectl delete --dry-run.translation: Simulate deleting resources from the cluster without actually removing anything.
kubectl delete --dry-run.rationale: No resources are deleted; only validates the request and shows what would be removed.

kubectl delete --force --grace-period=0.translation: Immediately remove resources from the cluster without waiting for graceful shutdown, forcibly terminating any running containers.
kubectl delete --force --grace-period=0.rationale: Bypasses graceful shutdown entirely, which can cause data corruption in stateful applications that need time to flush writes.

kubectl drain --delete-emptydir-data --f.translation: Evict all pods from a node for maintenance, including unmanaged pods and pods with local emptyDir data that will be permanently lost.
kubectl drain --delete-emptydir-data --f.rationale: Combines forced eviction with data loss acceptance, removing all workloads from a node including those with non-recoverable local data.

kubectl exec -it.translation: Open an interactive terminal session inside a running container, allowing direct command execution.
kubectl exec -it.rationale: Provides a live shell into a container where arbitrary commands can be run, potentially modifying application state or accessing sensitive data.

kubectl get --all-namespaces.translation: Display resources of the specified type from every namespace in the cluster in a single summary table.
kubectl get --all-namespaces.rationale: Read-only cluster-wide listing that provides a broader view without modifying anything.

kubectl logs -f.translation: Stream live log output from a container, continuously printing new lines as they are produced.
kubectl logs -f.rationale: Read-only log streaming that follows output in real time without modifying the container or cluster.

kubectl scale --replicas.translation: Set the exact number of running replicas for a deployment, replica set, or stateful set.
kubectl scale --replicas.rationale: Directly changes application capacity; setting replicas to zero effectively shuts down the application.

ln -f -s.translation: Create a symbolic link, overwriting any existing file at the destination without prompting.
ln -f -s.rationale: Silently replaces an existing file or link at the destination path to create the new symbolic link.

ln -s.translation: Create a symbolic link (shortcut) that refers to an existing file or directory by path.
ln -s.rationale: Creates a lightweight pointer to a target; does not modify the target file or directory.

ls -R.translation: List the contents of a directory and all of its subdirectories recursively.
ls -R.rationale: Expands the listing to an entire directory tree; may produce large output but remains entirely read-only.

ls -a -l.translation: List all files in a directory including hidden ones, showing detailed information like permissions, size, and modification date.
ls -a -l.rationale: Combines detailed listing with hidden file visibility; entirely read-only.

ls -h -l.translation: List files with detailed information, showing file sizes in human-readable units like KB, MB, and GB.
ls -h -l.rationale: Combines detailed listing with human-readable sizes for easier scanning; entirely read-only.

make -j.translation: Build targets by running multiple Makefile commands simultaneously in parallel.
make -j.rationale: Increases build speed through parallelism without changing which commands are executed.

mv -f.translation: Move or rename files, overwriting any existing file at the destination without prompting for confirmation.
mv -f.rationale: Suppresses all confirmation prompts, silently replacing destination files.

mv -i.translation: Move or rename files, prompting for confirmation before overwriting any existing file at the destination.
mv -i.rationale: Interactive confirmation reduces the risk of accidentally overwriting important files.

mysql -e.translation: Execute a single SQL statement against a MySQL database and exit immediately.
mysql -e.rationale: Runs arbitrary SQL non-interactively, which may include destructive statements like DROP TABLE or DELETE without review.

mysql -p -u.translation: Connect to a MySQL database as a specified user, prompting for a password before establishing the session.
mysql -p -u.rationale: Standard authenticated connection pattern that ensures credentials are provided before any operations can be performed.

node --inspect.translation: Run a Node.js script with the Chrome DevTools debugger listening on the default port for remote inspection.
node --inspect.rationale: Opens a local debug port that allows stepping through code and inspecting state, but does not change program behavior.

node -e.translation: Evaluate a string of JavaScript code passed directly on the command line and execute it.
node -e.rationale: Runs arbitrary inline JavaScript that can perform any operation the runtime supports.

npm audit fix --dry-run.translation: Simulate fixing known vulnerabilities in installed packages, showing what would change without actually modifying anything.
npm audit fix --dry-run.rationale: No packages are installed or modified; only displays planned fixes.

npm audit fix --force.translation: Fix known vulnerabilities in installed packages by upgrading across major versions, which may introduce breaking API changes.
npm audit fix --force.rationale: Installs semver-major updates that may break existing code, and bypasses the default constraint of staying within compatible version ranges.

npm install --dry-run.translation: Simulate installing packages, showing what would be downloaded and changed without actually modifying the project.
npm install --dry-run.rationale: No packages are downloaded or installed; only displays the planned installation.

npm install --force.translation: Install packages while bypassing the local cache and overwriting existing packages, ignoring dependency conflict warnings.
npm install --force.rationale: Skips cache validation and forces installation of potentially incompatible dependencies, which may break the project.

npm install --force -g.translation: Force-install a package globally for all projects on this machine, bypassing the cache and overwriting any existing version.
npm install --force -g.rationale: Modifies the system-wide package directory while bypassing cache and dependency checks, potentially breaking other projects.

npm install --save-dev.translation: Install a package and record it as a development-only dependency in package.json.
npm install --save-dev.rationale: Downloads and executes code from the npm registry, adding it to devDependencies for use during development only.

npm publish --dry-run.translation: Simulate publishing a package to the npm registry, showing what files would be included without actually uploading.
npm publish --dry-run.rationale: No package is uploaded; only displays the contents and metadata that would be published.

npm unpublish --force.translation: Remove a package from the npm registry even outside the standard 72-hour safety window, breaking downstream projects that depend on it.
npm unpublish --force.rationale: Bypasses npm's safety restrictions to remove a published package, potentially breaking all projects that depend on that version.

pip install --upgrade.translation: Download and install the latest version of specified Python packages, replacing any currently installed versions.
pip install --upgrade.rationale: Upgrades packages to the latest version, which may introduce breaking API changes or incompatible dependencies.

pip install -r.translation: Download and install all Python packages listed in a requirements file from the package index.
pip install -r.rationale: Installs potentially many packages at once based on a file, executing arbitrary setup code for each during installation.

pip3 install --force-reinstall.translation: Download and reinstall Python packages even if they are already installed at the correct version, re-running all setup scripts.
pip3 install --force-reinstall.rationale: Forces re-download and reinstallation of all packages, re-executing setup scripts that may have system-level side effects.

pip3 install --upgrade.translation: Download and install the latest version of a Python package, replacing any already-installed version.
pip3 install --upgrade.rationale: Replaces existing packages with newer versions that may introduce breaking changes or run new setup scripts.

pip3 install --user.translation: Download and install Python packages into the current user's site-packages directory instead of the system-wide location.
pip3 install --user.rationale: Downloads and runs code from PyPI but limits the installation to the user directory, avoiding system-wide changes.

pip3 install -e.translation: Install a local Python project in editable mode, linking its source directory into site-packages so code changes take effect immediately.
pip3 install -e.rationale: Runs setup scripts and creates a link to local source code; changes to the source are reflected without reinstalling.

pip3 install -r.translation: Download and install all Python packages listed in a requirements file and their dependencies.
pip3 install -r.rationale: Installs potentially many packages at once from a file, widening the scope of code downloaded and executed from PyPI.

pip3 uninstall -y.translation: Remove installed Python packages immediately without prompting for confirmation.
pip3 uninstall -y.rationale: Bypasses the interactive confirmation prompt, removing packages without a chance to review the list.

pnpm add --save-dev.translation: Download and install a package from the registry as a development-only dependency, updating package.json and the lockfile.
pnpm add --save-dev.rationale: Fetches and installs remote code that runs install scripts, categorized as a dev dependency so it is excluded from production builds.

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile.translation: Install all project dependencies from the registry, failing immediately if the lockfile would need any changes.
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile.rationale: Downloads and executes install scripts from remote packages but enforces lockfile immutability for reproducible builds.

prettier --check.translation: Check whether source code files are already formatted according to style rules without modifying them.
prettier --check.rationale: Read-only validation commonly used in CI pipelines to enforce consistent formatting.

prettier --write.translation: Format source code files in place, overwriting them with consistently styled output.
prettier --write.rationale: Rewrites files with purely stylistic changes that are trivially reversible via version control.

psql -c.translation: Execute a single SQL command against a PostgreSQL database and exit immediately.
psql -c.rationale: Runs arbitrary SQL non-interactively, which may include destructive statements like DROP TABLE or DELETE without review.

psql -f.translation: Execute all SQL commands from a file against a PostgreSQL database and exit.
psql -f.rationale: Runs an entire script that may contain multiple destructive operations, with limited opportunity to review each statement.

pytest --cov -v.translation: Run Python tests with verbose output and code coverage measurement for the specified package.
pytest --cov -v.rationale: Combines verbose output with coverage instrumentation for detailed test reporting.

pytest --lf -x.translation: Rerun only the tests that failed in the last session, stopping on the first new failure.
pytest --lf -x.rationale: Focuses on previously failing tests and exits early, enabling a fast red-green debugging loop.

pytest --pdb -x.translation: Run Python tests, stopping on the first failure and dropping into the Python debugger to inspect the error.
pytest --pdb -x.rationale: Stops early and opens an interactive debugger session, useful for diagnosing test failures.

python3 -c.translation: Execute a Python command string passed directly on the command line.
python3 -c.rationale: Runs arbitrary inline code that can perform any operation the interpreter supports.

python3 -m.translation: Run a Python library module as a standalone script.
python3 -m.rationale: Executes a module's __main__ entry point, which may install packages, start servers, or modify files.

python3 -u.translation: Run the Python 3 interpreter with unbuffered standard output and error streams for real-time logging.
python3 -u.rationale: Ensures output appears immediately rather than being batched, useful for long-running scripts.

redis-cli --pipe.translation: Stream raw Redis protocol commands from standard input to the server in bulk for high-throughput ingestion.
redis-cli --pipe.rationale: Sends arbitrary commands at wire speed without per-command review, which may include destructive operations like FLUSHDB.

redis-cli -h -p.translation: Connect to a Redis data store on a specified remote host and port.
redis-cli -h -p.rationale: Establishes a connection to a remote Redis instance where any command can be executed.

rm -I -r.translation: Recursively delete a directory tree, prompting once for confirmation before proceeding with the bulk deletion.
rm -I -r.rationale: Provides a single confirmation prompt before irreversibly destroying an entire directory hierarchy.

rm -f.translation: Delete files without prompting for confirmation, silently ignoring files that do not exist.
rm -f.rationale: Suppresses all confirmation prompts and errors for missing files, but the blast radius is limited to explicitly named files.

rm -i.translation: Delete files, prompting for explicit confirmation before each individual file is removed.
rm -i.rationale: Interactive confirmation before every deletion provides strong protection against accidental removal.

rm -r.translation: Recursively delete a directory and everything inside it, prompting for confirmation on read-only files.
rm -r.rationale: Destroys entire directory trees, which is effectively irreversible without backups.

rm -rf.translation: Recursively delete an entire directory tree and all its contents without prompting for confirmation, even for read-only files.
rm -rf.rationale: Silently and irreversibly destroys entire directory hierarchies with no confirmation or recovery mechanism.

ruff check --fix.translation: Analyze Python source code for lint errors and automatically fix all problems that have safe corrections.
ruff check --fix.rationale: Modifies source files in place but only applies auto-fix rules that are considered safe by default.

ruff format --check.translation: Check whether Python source files are already formatted without modifying them.
ruff format --check.rationale: Read-only validation commonly used in CI pipelines to enforce consistent formatting.

scp -i.translation: Copy files between the local machine and a remote server over SSH, authenticating with a specified private key file.
scp -i.rationale: Transfers files using key-based authentication, which may access privileged remote accounts.

scp -r.translation: Recursively copy entire directory trees between the local machine and a remote server over SSH.
scp -r.rationale: Transfers full directory structures, increasing the volume of files that may be overwritten at the destination.

sed -E.translation: Find and replace text using extended regular expression syntax, printing results to the terminal.
sed -E.rationale: Changes only the regex dialect used for pattern matching; output goes to the terminal without modifying files.

sed -e -i.translation: Apply a specified editing command to files, modifying them directly on disk.
sed -e -i.rationale: Combines an explicit editing expression with in-place modification, permanently altering file contents.

sed -i.translation: Find and replace text or apply editing rules, modifying each file directly on disk instead of printing to the terminal.
sed -i.rationale: Overwrites original files in place with no automatic backup, permanently altering their contents.

sed -n.translation: Process input through editing rules but only print lines that are explicitly selected, suppressing all other output.
sed -n.rationale: Filters output without modifying any files; commonly used with the p command to extract specific lines.

sqlite3 -cmd.translation: Open a SQLite database and execute a specified SQL or dot-command before entering interactive mode.
sqlite3 -cmd.rationale: Runs an initial command that may modify the database before presenting the interactive prompt.

sqlite3 -csv.translation: Open a SQLite database and format all query output as comma-separated values.
sqlite3 -csv.rationale: Standard read-friendly output mode used for data export; does not change what queries can be executed.

ssh -L.translation: Create an SSH tunnel that forwards a local port to a remote address, allowing local applications to reach remote services securely.
ssh -L.rationale: Opens a local listening port that routes traffic through the encrypted SSH connection to a remote destination.

ssh -L -N.translation: Create an SSH port-forwarding tunnel without opening a remote shell, keeping the connection alive solely for traffic forwarding.
ssh -L -N.rationale: Opens a local-to-remote tunnel without executing commands, but still exposes a remote network path through the local port.

ssh -i.translation: Open a secure shell connection to a remote server, authenticating with a specified private key file.
ssh -i.rationale: Establishes a remote session using key-based authentication, which may access privileged accounts.

tar -c -f -z.translation: Create a new gzip-compressed archive containing the specified files and directories.
tar -c -f -z.rationale: Bundles files into a compressed archive without modifying the source files.

tar -f -t.translation: List the contents of an archive file without extracting anything.
tar -f -t.rationale: Displays archive contents as a read-only operation; no files are created or modified on disk.

tar -f -x.translation: Extract all files from an archive to the current directory.
tar -f -x.rationale: Writes extracted files to disk, potentially overwriting existing files at the destination.

tar -f -x -z.translation: Extract all files from a gzip-compressed archive to the current directory.
tar -f -x -z.rationale: Decompresses and extracts files to disk, potentially overwriting existing files at the destination.

terraform apply -auto-approve.translation: Create or update cloud infrastructure immediately without waiting for interactive confirmation, applying all planned changes at once.
terraform apply -auto-approve.rationale: Modifies live infrastructure with no confirmation prompt, removing the last guardrail before potentially destructive changes take effect.

terraform apply -auto-approve -destroy.translation: Destroy all managed cloud infrastructure immediately without confirmation, equivalent to terraform destroy -auto-approve.
terraform apply -auto-approve -destroy.rationale: Permanently deletes all managed resources with no confirmation prompt, combining the most destructive operation with the removal of all safeguards.

terraform apply -auto-approve -lock=fals.translation: Create or update cloud infrastructure immediately without confirmation and without acquiring the state lock.
terraform apply -auto-approve -lock=fals.rationale: Removes both the confirmation prompt and state locking safeguards, maximizing the risk of unintended changes and state corruption.

terraform apply -lock=false.translation: Create or update cloud infrastructure without acquiring the state lock, allowing other operations to run concurrently.
terraform apply -lock=false.rationale: Concurrent modifications without locking can corrupt the state file, causing Terraform to lose track of managed resources.

terraform destroy -auto-approve.translation: Destroy all managed cloud infrastructure immediately without waiting for interactive confirmation.
terraform destroy -auto-approve.rationale: Permanently deletes all managed resources including compute, databases, and networking with no confirmation prompt.

terraform destroy -auto-approve -lock=fa.translation: Destroy all managed cloud infrastructure immediately without confirmation and without acquiring the state lock.
terraform destroy -auto-approve -lock=fa.rationale: Combines immediate destruction with no locking, risking permanent data loss and state corruption in a single operation.

terraform destroy -lock=false.translation: Destroy all managed cloud infrastructure without acquiring the state lock, allowing other operations to run concurrently.
terraform destroy -lock=false.rationale: Combines infrastructure destruction with concurrent state access, risking both data loss and state corruption simultaneously.

terraform init -upgrade.translation: Reinitialize the Terraform working directory and upgrade all provider plugins and modules to the latest allowed versions.
terraform init -upgrade.rationale: Downloads newer provider versions that may introduce breaking changes or alter infrastructure behavior on the next apply.

terraform plan -destroy.translation: Generate an execution plan showing what Terraform would delete if a destroy were run, without actually destroying anything.
terraform plan -destroy.rationale: Read-only preview of destruction that helps verify which resources would be removed before committing to a destroy.

terraform state push -force.translation: Upload a local state file to the remote backend, overwriting it even if the lineage or serial number does not match.
terraform state push -force.rationale: Bypasses all state consistency checks, risking total corruption of the shared state that tracks all managed infrastructure.

tsc --noEmit.translation: Type-check TypeScript source code without writing any compiled JavaScript output files.
tsc --noEmit.rationale: Read-only validation commonly used in CI pipelines to catch type errors without producing build artifacts.

tsc --watch.translation: Compile TypeScript source code and continuously recompile whenever source files change.
tsc --watch.rationale: Keeps the compiler running as a long-lived process that rebuilds on file changes, standard for development workflows.

yarn add --dev.translation: Download and install a package from the registry as a development-only dependency, updating package.json and the lockfile.
yarn add --dev.rationale: Fetches and installs remote code that runs install scripts, categorized as a dev dependency so it is excluded from production builds.

yarn install --frozen-lockfile.translation: Install all project dependencies from the registry, failing immediately if the lockfile would need any changes.
yarn install --frozen-lockfile.rationale: Downloads and executes install scripts from remote packages but enforces lockfile immutability for reproducible builds.

yarn upgrade --latest.translation: Update all project dependencies to their absolute latest versions, ignoring the semver ranges specified in package.json.
yarn upgrade --latest.rationale: Bypasses version range constraints and may introduce major breaking changes across multiple packages at once.
